items.body:
## Feature Request

Add UI zoom/scale controls for the desktop app.

## Problem

The default font size and UI elements are too small on some displays, making it hard to read and interact with the interface. Users with high-DPI screens or vision needs have no way to adjust the scale.

## Proposed Solution

- Add zoom in/out controls (keyboard shortcuts like `Ctrl+=` / `Ctrl+-` / `Ctrl+0`)
- Or a slider in settings to adjust UI scale (e.g., 80% - 150%)
- Persist the zoom level across sessions

## Alternatives Considered

- OS-level display scaling works but affects all apps, not just Hermes
- Browser zoom (`Ctrl+scroll`) doesn't apply to Electron/TUI apps

## Context

- Platform: Windows 10
- Runtime: Hermes desktop GUI app (Electron-based)

items.title: Gateway: MCP stdio subprocesses accumulate as zombies on restart

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Description

Each `hermes gateway restart` spawns a new MCP stdio subprocess. When the gateway shuts down, the MCP subprocess is not reaped. After restart, orphaned processes are reparented to PID 1 (init) but never reaped, becoming `<defunct>` zombies.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start gateway with `mcp_servers` configured (stdio transport, e.g. Mimir)
2. Run `hermes gateway restart` multiple times
3. Observe `ps aux | grep mimir` — zombie count grows with each restart

## Actual

```
$ ps aux | grep mimir | grep defunct | wc -l
57
$ ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,comm | grep mimir | head -3
3813       1 Z    mimir
5667       1 Z    mimir
6219       1 Z    mimir
```

All zombies have PPID=1 (reparented to init after gateway parent exited without reaping).

## Impact

Zombies accumulate over time. After 10+ restarts: 50-100 zombie entries. While resource cost is negligible (just a PID slot), they clutter process listings and can exhaust PID namespace on systems with low `pid_max`.

## Expected

Gateway shutdown should terminate and `wait()` MCP stdio subprocesses. No zombie accumulation.

## Possible Fixes

- Properly terminate + wait MCP subprocesses during gateway shutdown
- Use `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` on Linux so subprocess dies with parent
- Startup cleanup pass to reap orphaned MCP processes from prior runs

## Environment

Hermes Agent gateway in Docker on Unraid 7.3.1. Mimir v1.0.0 as MCP server (stdio). Container init: bash (PID 1), not tini or another auto-reaping init.

items.title: [Feature]: Slack: render clarify choices as Block Kit buttons (counterpart to Discord #19111)
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

On Slack, the clarify tool's multiple-choice questions render as a numbered plain-text list — the user reads the options and types "2" back into the channel. On Discord and Telegram the same prompt renders as tappable buttons (Discord shipped this in #19111 / #25485, commit 1dca6a6; WhatsApp also has it). Slack is the only major adapter still on the text fallback.

This is one of the concrete, narrow Slack items the maintainer named when the Slack Block Kit umbrella (#34587) was closed as not planned:

> "clarify-as-buttons (Slack counterpart to #19111) ... each a clean standalone issue. If you want to drive any of them, please open them as individual tickets."

Filing it as that standalone ticket.

### Proposed Solution

Override `BasePlatformAdapter.send_clarify` on `SlackAdapter` (`gateway/platforms/slack.py`), reusing the Block Kit + inbound-action + auth infrastructure that already powers `send_exec_approval` and `send_slash_confirm`.

- **Multi-choice:** a `section` block (the question) + an `actions` block with one button per choice plus a trailing "✏️ Other" button. Button value encodes `clarify_id|index`. For choice lists longer than Slack's 5-per-row action cap, render a single `static_select` instead (mirrors WhatsApp's 1–3 buttons / 4+ list split in `whatsapp_cloud.py:658`).
- **Inbound handler:** numeric click → `tools.clarify_gateway.resolve_gateway_clarify(clarify_id, canonical_choice_text)`; "Other" → `mark_awaiting_text(clarify_id)` so the gateway's existing text-intercept captures the next in-thread message. Canonical choice text is round-tripped from the clarify entry, not the button label (mirrors the Discord implementation).
- Reuse the existing fail-closed auth (`_is_interactive_user_authorized`) and in-thread posting (`_resolve_thread_ts`); single-use disable + context footer on resolution, like the approval flow.
- **Open-ended** clarify calls (no `choices`) keep rendering as plain text — unchanged.
- 3000-char section-block budget so long questions don't trip `invalid_blocks` (same guard as `send_exec_approval`).

No changes to `base.py` or the gateway `clarify_callback` — that scaffolding already drives every adapter; Slack inherits the text fallback today and gains buttons via this override. Same footprint as the merged Discord change (commit 1dca6a6).

### Alternatives Considered

- Wait for the generic platform-agnostic action-button API (#15311, open). Not chosen: that's a larger future layer with no committed direction, and the per-adapter `send_clarify` override is the shipped, maintainer-merged pattern (Discord #25485). If #15311 lands later, clarify can be re-pointed at it.
- Copy Feishu's interactive-card approach (`feishu.py`). Not chosen: Feishu routes clicks as synthetic COMMAND events rather than via `resolve_gateway_clarify`, which diverges from the `clarify_callback` contract the gateway expects.
- ReplyKeyboard-style "type the number" UX. That's the current text fallback — the whole point is to remove it on a platform that supports native buttons.

### Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR (PR #28885 is open).

items.title: [Bug]: `hermes config set` silently coerces enum string values "off"/"on" to Python booleans, corrupting schema-validated enum settings

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

`hermes config set` silently coerces the literal strings `off`/`on`/`yes`/`no`/`true`/`false` to Python booleans when writing to `config.yaml`, with no `--type` flag or other escape hatch. This corrupts any setting whose schema declares a string-typed enum containing one of those tokens.

Concrete case: `hermes config set approvals.mode off` writes `mode: false` instead of `mode: 'off'`. The Desktop settings UI then renders a fourth option labeled "False" that isn't in the schema, and selects it as the current value.

This is a CLI bug, not a Desktop bug. The Desktop schema is correct (`['manual', 'smart', 'off']`); the CLI silently fed it a value the schema can't parse.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes config set approvals.mode off` (or any value matching the coercion set: `on`, `yes`, `no`, `true`, `false`).
2. Inspect `~/.hermes/config.yaml` — the line is `mode: false`, not `mode: 'off'`.
3. Open Hermes Desktop → Settings → Permissions → **Approval Mode** dropdown.
4. Observe: the dropdown shows four options (Manual, Smart, Off, **False**); "False" is selected as the current value.

## Expected Behavior

Any of the following would be acceptable:

- `--type {auto,str,int,float,bool}` flag (defaulting to `auto`, i.e. today's behavior) so users can force `hermes config set approvals.mode --type str off`.
- Schema-aware coercion: if the target key is a string-typed enum per the Desktop schema, skip bool/int/float coercion and store the literal string.
- Refuse ambiguous values with a clear error: `error: 'off' is ambiguous (bool False or string 'off'); pass --type str to force the string`.

## Actual Behavior

The CLI hard-codes a coercion table (`hermes_cli/config.py:6287-6295`) that maps `off`/`on`/`yes`/`no`/`true`/`false` to Python `True`/`False` regardless of the target schema. The corrupted value passes validation because YAML is technically valid; the schema mismatch surfaces only at UI render time as a phantom dropdown option.

## Affected Component

- [x] Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

## Messaging Platform

- [x] N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

N/A — pure CLI bug, fully reproducible in one command, no gateway or log involvement.

## Operating System

macOS 26.5.1 (cross-platform — CLI is identical on Linux/Windows)

## Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream 36ae9584 — "Up to date"

## Root Cause Analysis

`hermes_cli/config.py:6287-6295`:

```python
# Convert value to appropriate type
if value.lower() in {'true', 'yes', 'on'}:
    value = True
elif value.lower() in {'false', 'no', 'off'}:
    value = False
elif value.isdigit():
    value = int(value)
elif value.replace('.', '', 1).isdigit():
    value = float(value)
```

The coercion block runs unconditionally after argparse, with no schema lookup and no user override. The schema for `approvals.mode` is declared at `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/constants.ts`:

```ts
'approvals.mode': ['manual', 'smart', 'off'],
```

— a string enum — but the CLI never consults it.

## Proposed Fix

Two complementary changes:

1. **Add a `--type` flag** to `hermes config set` accepting `{auto,str,int,float,bool}`. Default `auto` preserves current behavior. `str` skips all coercion and writes the literal value as a YAML string. Minimal CLI surface, maximum user control.

2. **Schema-aware coercion for known keys**: when the target key matches a string-typed enum in the schema (e.g., `approvals.mode`, `discord.reply_threading_mode`, future `*.mode` settings), default to `str` and emit a one-line warning if the user explicitly passed `--type bool`. This makes the safe path the default without forcing users to learn the flag.

The fix is contained to `hermes_cli/config.py`'s `cmd_config_set` flow; no schema or Desktop changes required.

## Related

- Caught while filing #47504 (Desktop profile dialog uppercase UX bug — fixed by #47511). The reproducer for that issue happened to trigger this one.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Regression: Ollama Cloud model switch keeps stale Codex base_url and sends deepseek-v4-pro to chatgpt.com endpoint

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

I believe this was introduced here:

 PR #8003 (commit 06f862fa1, 2026-04-11): feat(cli): add native /model picker modal for provider → model selection.


After switching from OpenAI Codex to Ollama Cloud and selecting `deepseek-v4-pro`, Hermes reports the active runtime as `Provider: ollama-cloud` and `Model: deepseek-v4-pro`, but the API request is still sent to the previous Codex endpoint:

```text
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
```

That endpoint mismatch causes immediate HTTP 404 failures. The provider/model switch appears to update the provider and model, but not the endpoint/base URL.

Pre-submit checks:

- Searched existing issues/PRs for this exact Ollama Cloud + Codex endpoint mismatch; did not find an exact duplicate.
- `hermes version` reports the install is up to date.
- Ran `hermes debug share` and included the redacted paste links below.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Hermes with the OpenAI Codex provider/model active, so the runtime endpoint is `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`.
2. Switch provider/model to Ollama Cloud, selecting `deepseek-v4-pro`.
3. Send a message.
4. Observe the request failure output.

A representative bad config/runtime state is:

```yaml
model:
  provider: ollama-cloud
  default: deepseek-v4-pro
  base_url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
```

## Expected Behavior

When `ollama-cloud` is selected, Hermes should send requests to the Ollama Cloud endpoint, for example:

```text
https://ollama.com/v1
```

or to an explicit `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` / valid configured Ollama endpoint.

Hermes should not reuse a stale endpoint from the previously selected Codex provider.

## Actual Behavior

Hermes reports the selected provider/model as Ollama Cloud / DeepSeek, but sends the request to the Codex endpoint:

```text
⚠️  API call failed (attempt 1/3): NotFoundError [HTTP 404]
   🔌 Provider: ollama-cloud  Model: deepseek-v4-pro
   🌐 Endpoint: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
   📝 Error: HTTP 404: Error code: 404 - {'detail': 'Not Found'}
   📋 Details: {'detail': 'Not Found'}
   ⏱️  Elapsed: 0.16s  Context: 2 msgs, ~4,974 tokens
```

## Affected Component

- CLI (interactive chat)
- Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)
- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/46UAH
agent.log    https://paste.rs/RkQ7B
gateway.log  https://paste.rs/HgWeu
```

Pastes were generated with redaction enabled via:

```shell
hermes debug share --lines 120 --expire 7
```

## Operating System

Linux 7.0.12-070012-generic x86_64

## Python Version

```text
Python 3.11.15 (Hermes venv)
Python 3.14.4 (system python3)
```

## Hermes Version

```text
Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream 36ae9584
Project: /home/tim/.hermes/hermes-agent
Python: 3.11.15
OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
Up to date
```

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
⚠️  API call failed (attempt 1/3): NotFoundError [HTTP 404]
   🔌 Provider: ollama-cloud  Model: deepseek-v4-pro
   🌐 Endpoint: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
   📝 Error: HTTP 404: Error code: 404 - {'detail': 'Not Found'}
   📋 Details: {'detail': 'Not Found'}
   ⏱️  Elapsed: 0.16s  Context: 2 msgs, ~4,974 tokens
```

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

This looks like a stale `model.base_url` leakage issue.

`model.base_url` is a single global config field. If it contains the previous provider's Codex endpoint and the provider/model switch updates `model.provider` to `ollama-cloud` without clearing or replacing `model.base_url`, runtime resolution can end up with:

```text
provider = ollama-cloud
model = deepseek-v4-pro
base_url = https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
```

Relevant areas appear to be:

- `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py`
- model switch persistence paths in `cli.py`
- gateway model switch persistence path in `gateway/slash_commands.py`

This appears related in theme to #44099 / #44070 (base_url drift), but it is not the same path: this failure occurs after provider/model switch, not after credential-pool recovery.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

Two complementary protections would prevent this:

1. When a provider/model switch is persisted, save the new provider's resolved base URL or clear `model.base_url` if no explicit endpoint should be persisted.
2. In runtime provider resolution, only honor `model.base_url` for built-in providers if the saved endpoint is compatible with the selected provider. For example, `ollama-cloud` should not accept `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` as its runtime endpoint. Provider-specific env vars such as `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` should still be honored.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Feature]: Cost & usage visibility / provider/routing UX

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Hermes currently estimates token costs when pricing metadata is available, but there is no obvious way for users to define their own per-token pricing for specific models/providers. This becomes a problem when:

Using local/custom endpoints that report usage tokens but don’t expose trustworthy cost metadata.
Running under special pricing plans where effective model rates differ from public/listed pricing.
Teams have negotiated enterprise rates, volume discounts, or promotional terms and want session cost reporting to match their actual bill.
Certain high-usage local/proxy setups need a consistent internal “internal cost floor/rate” for budgeting and cost governance.
As a result, /usage and cost estimates can be misleading or missing (unknown) even though token usage is correctly tracked.

### Proposed Solution

Add user-configurable token pricing overrides with first-class support in config + CLI so Hermes can calculate costs using actual intended pricing while keeping live-provider metadata as the default source.

1) Add pricing override configuration block
New optional config section in ~/.hermes/config.yaml:

pricing:
  custom_overrides:
    enabled: true
    currency: USD
    providers:
      - provider: custom            # or ollama-cloud, openrouter, etc.
        billing_mode: user_override
        models:
          - model: "llama3.3:70b"
            input_cost_per_million: 0.0
            output_cost_per_million: 0.0
            cache_read_cost_per_million: 0.0
            cache_write_cost_per_million: 0.0
            request_cost: 0.0
            reason: "internal-labs-promo"
          - model: "qwen2.5:14b"
            input_cost_per_million: 1.2
            output_cost_per_million: 4.8
            cache_read_cost_per_million: 0.3
            cache_write_cost_per_million: 0.3
            request_cost: 0.0
            effective_from: "2026-01-01"
            effective_until: "2026-12-31"
      - provider: "ollama-cloud"
        plan: "enterprise-2026"
        models:
          - model: "gemma-3-27b"
            input_cost_per_million: 0.7
            output_cost_per_million: 2.1
            request_cost: 0.0
Behavior

Matching precedence (proposed):
Exact model override in active provider/plan bucket
Provider fallback override
Provider metadata/source pricing
Unknown/zero fallback
Supports input, output, cache_read, cache_write, and optional fixed request_cost.
New cost source label "user_override" and "custom_contract" already exists in code, so this integrates cleanly as a first-class source.
2) CLI commands for overrides
Add commands so users can manage pricing quickly without editing YAML manually:

hermes pricing list
hermes pricing set --provider PROVIDER --model MODEL --input ... --output ...
hermes pricing set --provider PROVIDER --plan PLAN --model MODEL ...
hermes pricing remove --provider PROVIDER --model MODEL
hermes pricing import --file path/to/pricing.json
3) /usage and account-cost display
Update cost output to reflect override source clearly:

show cost label/source when custom pricing is used:
~$X for estimated
$X for actual/known
custom/contract badge or text for override source
Keep existing behavior unchanged when overrides are absent.
4) Persistence / schema / docs
Add config validation + migration docs.
Include in docs: provider pricing strategy, precedence rules, examples.
Add test cases in test_usage_command / pricing tests for:
local endpoint with usage + custom override
model-specific override
provider-wide override fallback
plan-scoped override precedence

### Alternatives Considered

Do everything manually outside Hermes (export session tokens, map with external spreadsheet script).

Doesn’t scale well and breaks the whole “in-session visibility” experience.
Depend only on provider metadata for cost estimation.

Fails for local/custom endpoints and special plan pricing where metadata is absent or incorrect.
Expose cost override only as a debug/insights plugin.

Useful but fragmented; native /usage and built-in reporting should stay authoritative and first-party.
This proposal is better because it keeps pricing logic centralized, improves cost transparency, and aligns with existing cost fields/usage tracking flow.

### Feature Type

Configuration option

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

items.title: Telegram typing indicator stuck infinitely (orphaned _keep_typing task)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Description

The Telegram typing indicator sometimes persists forever — 30+ minutes with no activity — after a session completes. /restart kills it immediately.

## Root Cause

In gateway/platforms/base.py, the _keep_typing asyncio task refreshes send_chat_action every 2s. Under certain edge cases the task cancellation in _stop_typing_task() does not take effect and the loop continues indefinitely as an orphaned task.

## Observed Behavior

- After a normal response, Telegram shows typing... forever
- No new messages — indicator flashes for 30+ minutes
- /restart immediately resolves it (kills orphaned task)
- Gateway otherwise processes messages normally

## Expected

Typing indicator stops within 5 seconds of response completion.

## Proposed Fix

Add a maximum duration watchdog to _keep_typing — auto-cancel after 5 minutes regardless of stop_event state.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.16.0 (latest main)
- macOS 26.5.1, Apple M4
- Python 3.11.15
- Telegram platform adapter

items.title: [Bug] Windows: scripts/install.ps1 venv recreation fails when pythonw.exe holds .pyd locks — only kills hermes.exe

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

When `scripts/install.ps1` recreates the venv on Windows (bootstrap installer or `hermes update` CLI path), it only kills `hermes.exe` processes before deleting the old venv — but **does not kill `python.exe` / `pythonw.exe` processes that are running from inside that same venv**. Those processes hold native extension `.pyd` files as loaded DLLs, which Windows locks. `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "venv"` then fails with "The directory is not empty" because the recursive deletion hits a locked file deep inside `site-packages/.../__pycache__/`.

## Observed failure

Bootstrap installer log:

```
Creating virtual environment with Python 3.11...
Virtual environment already exists, recreating...
venv: failed - Cannot remove item ...\venv\Lib\site-packages\lark_oapi\api\apaas\v1\model\__pycache__: The directory is not empty.
```

After manually killing the leftover `pythonw.exe` (PID 96968) from the old venv, the same `Remove-Item` succeeds.

A more verbose attempt revealed the underlying lock:

```
Remove-Item ...\venv\Lib\site-packages\tornado\speedups.pyd: Access to the path 'speedups.pyd' is denied.
```

This confirms the cascade: Python `.pyd` → loaded DLL → `Remove-Item -Recurse` fails halfway → `__pycache__` orphan → whole venv stage fails.

## Root cause

In `scripts/install.ps1` ~line 1436-1443:

```powershell
if (Test-Path "venv") {
    Write-Info "Virtual environment already exists, recreating..."
    if ($env:OS -eq "Windows_NT") {
        $myPid = $PID
        Write-Info "Stopping any running hermes processes before recreating venv..."
        & taskkill /F /T /IM hermes.exe /FI "PID ne $myPid" 2>$null | Out-Null
        # ^^^ only kills hermes.exe, but python.exe / pythonw.exe from the same venv
        #     can also hold .pyd locks!
        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 800
    }
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "venv"
}
```

The `taskkill` only targets `hermes.exe`. If there are any `python.exe` or `pythonw.exe` processes whose binary path points inside the old venv (e.g. spawned by the gateway), they will hold `.pyd` file locks and prevent recursive deletion.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows 10/11, install Hermes with gateway enabled
2. Start the gateway (`hermes gateway start`), which spawns `pythonw.exe` from the venv
3. Run `hermes update` or the bootstrap installer (which triggers venv recreation)
4. The gateway processes are stopped/restarted during the update, but `pythonw.exe` from the old venv may still be alive
5. `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "venv"` fails → installer fails → update fails

## Expected behavior

Before deleting the old venv, also kill any `python.exe` and `pythonw.exe` processes whose image path starts with the old venv directory. A rough PowerShell fix:

```powershell
if ($env:OS -eq "Windows_NT") {
    $myPid = $PID
    & taskkill /F /T /IM hermes.exe /FI "PID ne $myPid" 2>$null | Out-Null
    # Also kill python/w processes that live in the old venv
    Get-Process python*,pythonw* -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {
        $_.Path -like "$InstallDir\venv\*"
    } | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 800
}
```

## Related issues

- #43268 covers a similar lock-contention problem but focuses on the Desktop auto-update path and the `hermes.exe` / `brotlicffi.pyd` locks specifically.
- #46791 covers the fragile git stash handling during updates (including the `nul` file issue on Windows), which compounds the problem by forcing fallback to the ZIP download path that hits the same lock.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 AMD64
- Python: 3.11.15 (venv)
- Hermes: v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)
- Install: git clone + pip install (managed by `hermes update` / bootstrap installer)
- Install path: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent`

items.title: clarify: typed replies to button prompts fall through instead of resolving the clarify — intended?

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Context

When the gateway has a pending clarify that presents **button / multiple-choice** options, a user who *types* an answer instead of tapping a button has their message dropped from the clarify flow. `get_pending_for_session()` only returns clarifies with `awaiting_text=True`, so a typed reply to a button prompt isn't intercepted as the clarify answer — it falls through to normal dispatch and is handled as a new turn / interrupt of the still-blocked agent.

This looks intentional (references as of `5e01a5dbf`):

- `tools/clarify_gateway.py` — `register(...)` sets `awaiting_text=not bool(choices)`, and `get_pending_for_session()` returns only `awaiting_text` entries; a button clarify flips to text mode only via `mark_awaiting_text()` (the "Other" path).
- `gateway/run.py` — the intercept comment says it captures text only for clarifies *"awaiting free-form text (either an open-ended clarify … or one where the user picked the 'Other' button)."*
- Tests encode it: `test_button_choice_does_not_auto_await` (`get_pending_for_session(...) is None` for a button clarify) and `test_other_button_flips_to_text_mode`.

### The UX gap

On chat platforms (Telegram, in our case) users frequently type a fuller, free-form answer rather than tapping one of the offered buttons — e.g. the prompt offers **A / B / C** and the user types *"do B, but only for staging."* Today that message does not resolve the clarify: the agent stays blocked on the clarify until it times out, while the typed message is processed separately as an interrupt. From the user's side it looks like the bot ignored their answer.

### Proposal

Would you accept making a typed (non-slash) reply resolve the **oldest pending** clarify for a session even when it's a button/multiple-choice prompt — with button taps still resolving via the callback exactly as they do today?

To preserve the current default and keep the existing tests green, I'd implement it **behind a config flag** (e.g. `clarify.text_resolves_button_prompts`, default `false`), add tests for the opt-in path, and update the call-site comment + docs. Slash commands would continue to fall through.

Happy to open the PR if this direction is acceptable — or to adjust (always-on vs flag, naming, scope) to your preference.

items.title: [BUG] WeCom adapter: WebSocket reconnection may fail silently without logging success or failure

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

After a WeCom WebSocket connection error, the adapter's reconnection logic may fail silently without logging success or failure. This creates ambiguity about whether the connection was actually restored, leading to potential message loss and debugging difficulties.

## Environment

- OS: WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04 on Windows 11)
- Hermes Agent version: latest main
- Platform: WeCom (企业微信) AI Bot WebSocket
- Affected component: `gateway/platforms/wecom.py` line 334-359

## Observed Behavior

### Log sequence from production incident (2026-06-17):

```
10:05:38 ERROR gateway.platforms.wecom: [Wecom] Send failed: send reply markdown failed: 
  WeCom errcode 846609: aibot websocket not subscribed

10:06:08 WARNING gateway.platforms.wecom: [Wecom] WebSocket error: WeCom websocket closed

[NO FURTHER LOGS - No "Reconnected" or "Reconnect failed" messages]
```

Expected log sequence should include one of:
- `INFO [Wecom] Reconnected` (success)
- `WARNING [Wecom] Reconnect failed: <error>` (failure)
- Stack trace if exception occurred

But neither appears, suggesting the reconnection logic either:
1. Hung indefinitely in `_open_connection()`
2. Succeeded but `_mark_connected()` didn't log
3. Failed without raising an exception

## Root Cause Analysis

### Reconnection logic in _listen_loop (line 334-359):

```python
async def _listen_loop(self) -> None:
    backoff_idx = 0
    while self._running:
        try:
            await self._read_events()
            backoff_idx = 0
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            return
        except Exception as exc:
            if not self._running:
                return
            logger.warning("[%s] WebSocket error: %s", self.name, exc)
            self._fail_pending_responses(RuntimeError("WeCom connection interrupted"))

            delay = RECONNECT_BACKOFF[min(backoff_idx, len(RECONNECT_BACKOFF) - 1)]
            backoff_idx += 1
            await asyncio.sleep(delay)

            try:
                await self._open_connection()  # ← May hang or fail silently
                backoff_idx = 0
                self._mark_connected()
                logger.info("[%s] Reconnected", self.name)  # ← Never logged
            except Exception as reconnect_exc:
                logger.warning("[%s] Reconnect failed: %s", self.name, reconnect_exc)
```

### _open_connection() (line 281-309):

```python
async def _open_connection(self) -> None:
    await self._cleanup_ws()
    self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(trust_env=True)
    self._ws = await self._session.ws_connect(
        self._ws_url,
        heartbeat=HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS * 2,
        timeout=CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,  # 20 seconds
    )

    req_id = self._new_req_id("subscribe")
    await self._send_json({
        "cmd": APP_CMD_SUBSCRIBE,
        "headers": {"req_id": req_id},
        "body": {
            "bot_id": self._bot_id,
            "secret": self._secret,
            "device_id": self._device_id,
        },
    })

    auth_payload = await self._wait_for_handshake(req_id)  # ← May hang
    errcode = auth_payload.get("errcode", 0)
    if errcode not in {0, None}:
        errmsg = auth_payload.get("errmsg", "authentication failed")
        raise RuntimeError(f"{errmsg} (errcode={errcode})")
```

### Potential silent failure points:

1. **_wait_for_handshake() may hang indefinitely**
   - Line 315: `deadline = asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`
   - But if `self._ws.receive()` blocks forever, deadline is never checked
   - No explicit timeout on the `receive()` call

2. **_send_json() may fail without raising**
   - Line 421-425: Checks `self._ws.closed` but not other error states
   - If connection dropped mid-send, exception may be swallowed

3. **_mark_connected() doesn't log**
   - Inherited from base adapter, no logging statement
   - Success case has no confirmation

4. **Exception may not be caught properly**
   - If `_open_connection()` raises `CancelledError`, it's caught by outer handler
   - But if it raises `asyncio.TimeoutError`, it should be caught by inner handler
   - No stack trace logged, suggesting exception handling issue

## Impact

- **Debugging difficulty**: Cannot determine if connection was restored
- **Message loss**: If reconnection failed silently, all subsequent sends will fail
- **Operational blind spot**: No monitoring/alerting possible without logs
- **Severity**: Medium. Affects observability and debugging, not core functionality

## Proposed Fix

### 1. Add explicit timeout to _wait_for_handshake()

```python
async def _wait_for_handshake(self, req_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    deadline = asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
    while True:
        remaining = deadline - asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
        if remaining <= 0:
            raise asyncio.TimeoutError(f"Handshake timeout after {CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s")
        
        try:
            msg = await asyncio.wait_for(self._ws.receive(), timeout=remaining)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            raise asyncio.TimeoutError(f"Handshake timeout after {CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s")
        
        if msg.type == aiohttp.WSMsgType.TEXT:
            payload = self._parse_json(msg.data)
            if payload and self._payload_req_id(payload) == req_id:
                return payload
        elif msg.type in {aiohttp.WSMsgType.CLOSED, aiohttp.WSMsgType.ERROR}:
            raise RuntimeError("WebSocket closed during handshake")
```

### 2. Add logging to _mark_connected()

```python
def _mark_connected(self) -> None:
    super()._mark_connected()
    logger.info("[%s] Connection state updated: connected", self.name)
```

### 3. Add comprehensive logging in _listen_loop reconnection

```python
try:
    logger.info("[%s] Attempting reconnection (backoff: %ds)...", self.name, delay)
    await self._open_connection()
    backoff_idx = 0
    self._mark_connected()
    logger.info("[%s] Reconnected successfully", self.name)
except asyncio.TimeoutError as exc:
    logger.error("[%s] Reconnect timeout: %s", self.name, exc)
except asyncio.CancelledError:
    logger.info("[%s] Reconnect cancelled", self.name)
    raise
except Exception as reconnect_exc:
    logger.error("[%s] Reconnect failed: %s", self.name, reconnect_exc, exc_info=True)
```

### 4. Add health check after reconnection

```python
await self._open_connection()
self._mark_connected()

# Verify connection is actually working
try:
    await self._send_json({"cmd": APP_CMD_PING, "headers": {"req_id": "ping-test"}, "body": {}})
    logger.info("[%s] Reconnected and health check passed", self.name)
except Exception as exc:
    logger.error("[%s] Reconnected but health check failed: %s", self.name, exc)
    raise
```

## Reproduction Steps

1. Start gateway with WeCom adapter
2. Force a WebSocket disconnection (network interruption, server restart)
3. Observe logs for reconnection messages
4. Expected: See "Reconnected" or "Reconnect failed" within 2-62 seconds
5. Actual: May see neither, creating ambiguity

## Additional Context

- `RECONNECT_BACKOFF = [2, 5, 10, 30, 60]` - exponential backoff strategy
- `CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 20.0` - intended timeout but may not be enforced
- Similar pattern may exist in other WebSocket adapters (QQBot, DingTalk, Feishu)
- Related to issue #47564 (846609 error handling)

## Willing to Submit PR

Yes. I can submit a PR with the proposed logging improvements and timeout enforcement.

---

Discovered during production debugging on 2026-06-17. Incident logs show gap between "WebSocket error" and absence of reconnection confirmation.

items.title: Sandbox environment reliability: PATH shadowing and HOME path resolution
items.body:
## Problems

Two issues stem from the same root: the Hermes sandbox environment doesn't faithfully represent the user's real environment.

### Problem A: PATH priority — Homebrew tools shadowed by system

On macOS, `path_helper` builds PATH by reading `/etc/paths` first, then `/etc/paths.d/*`. Since `/usr/bin` is in `/etc/paths` and `/opt/homebrew/bin` is in `/etc/paths.d/homebrew`, system Python (3.9) shadows Homebrew Python (3.14). This breaks `tomllib` (stdlib, Python 3.11+) and any other dependency that requires a newer Python than the system provides.

Hermes's own venv has Python 3.11+, but any subprocess that calls bare `python3` hits the system version. DecisionFrame registration fails silently and falls back to a degraded mode.

### Problem B: HOME path — Cron sandbox HOME breaks Path.home()

Hermes cron jobs run with `HOME=~/.hermes/home` (sandbox) instead of the real user HOME. Python's `Path.home()` returns the sandbox path, so scripts that reference `Path.home() / ".hermes" / "skills"` resolve to a non-existent sandbox path.

Current workaround: every affected script manually detects and corrects the HOME path with a guard pattern. This doesn't scale.

Both problems share the same root: **the sandbox environment is not a faithful representation of the real environment.** Users must manually bridge paths, reorder PATH, or write guards in every script.

## Proposal

### 1. `hermes env check` — Standard environment dependency check

- Probe: Python version, PATH ordering, key module availability
- Output: OK / Warning / Blocking
- Should be run automatically after `hermes gateway install`
- Skills could declare required environment (e.g., `python >= 3.11`)
- Missing dependencies -> suggest isolated installs (venv), don't modify user's system environment

### 2. Sandbox HOME transparency

- `hermes gateway install` should detect when sandbox HOME is isolated from real HOME
- Automatically bridge `.hermes/` directory (at minimum) so `Path.home()` transparently resolves to real HOME for Hermes-owned paths
- Extend `hermes doctor` to cover PATH ordering and HOME path checks

### 3. Declarative dependency manifest

Skills should be able to declare:
```yaml
requires:
  python: ">= 3.11"
  modules: ["tomllib", "exchangelib"]
```

`hermes env check` would aggregate and validate these declarations.

## Design principles

- **Isolated installs**: Fix environments in the sandbox/venv, never modify the user's system config
- **Fail loud, not silent**: Missing dependencies should surface as errors with actionable paths, not degrade silently
- **Knowledge feedback**: Detected gaps should feed into the agent's knowledge base for future recall

items.title: Curator rollback to the oldest snapshot fails and deletes that snapshot

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
**Affected Component:** Skills (skill loading, hub, guard)

### What happened
When I roll back to the oldest curator snapshot, the rollback fails and that snapshot gets deleted. Before restoring, `rollback()` takes a safety snapshot of the current skills tree, and that path runs the normal prune step. When the backups directory is already at the keep limit (5 by default), the prune removes the oldest snapshot, which is the exact one I asked to restore. The extract then has nothing to read, so rollback returns "snapshot extract failed (state restored)" and my earliest restore point is gone.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Keep curator backups on, which is the default, with the default keep of 5.
2. Let the curator snapshot until the backups directory holds 5, which is its steady state. The oldest of those is the earliest restore point.
3. Run `hermes curator rollback --id <oldest snapshot id>`, picking the oldest one listed by `hermes curator rollback --list`.
4. The rollback fails with "snapshot extract failed (state restored)", and the oldest snapshot directory is now gone.

### Expected
Restoring any listed snapshot should succeed and leave that snapshot in place. Restoring a snapshot should never delete it.

### Actual
Rollback to the oldest snapshot fails, and that snapshot is permanently removed.

### Root cause (from reading the code)
In `agent/curator_backup.py`, `rollback()` takes a safety snapshot through `snapshot_skills()`, which ends by calling `_prune_old(keep=get_keep())`. That prune keeps the newest `keep` snapshots and deletes the rest, with no awareness of the rollback target. The safety snapshot is the newest one, so at the steady keep limit the oldest snapshot, which is the target, falls outside the window and is deleted before `rollback()` opens its `skills.tar.gz`.

### Impact
The live skills tree is preserved, because rollback moves it into a staging area and puts it back when the extract fails, so this is not loss of current skill data. What is lost is the oldest restore point itself, and the rollback I asked for does not happen. That restore point is often the most valuable one, because the curator takes a snapshot before each consolidation pass that can archive skills, so the oldest snapshot is the closest thing to a clean state from before the curator started changing things.

### Debug Report
N/A. I reproduced this from a clean source checkout with a standalone pytest regression rather than from a live session. The regression is included in the linked PR.

### Environment
Reproduced from a clean checkout of `main` at commit 5e01a5d. It is pure file and timestamp logic, so it shows up on every operating system.

items.title: Gateway/TUI session build (_make_agent) lacks the init-time provider fallback that cron and the CLI have — new sessions hard-fail with "No Codex credentials stored" instead of using fallback_model

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

A new TUI/gateway session hard-fails at init with `agent init failed: No Codex credentials stored. Run `hermes auth` to authenticate.` when the configured primary provider's auth fails, **instead of degrading to the configured `fallback_model` / `fallback_providers` chain**.

The cron scheduler and the classic CLI both perform this init-time fallback; the gateway's agent-build path (`tui_gateway/server.py` → `_make_agent`) does not. The result is an asymmetry users actually hit: **old / in-flight sessions fall back fine** (the conversation loop has its own fallback), but **every new session started after the primary loses auth errors out**.

Observed on `0.15.1`, but the relevant code paths look unchanged on main as of June 2026.

## Repro

Config (pro-style) with an OAuth primary and an API-key fallback:

```yaml
model:
  default: gpt-5.5
  provider: openai-codex
fallback_model:
  provider: deepseek
  model: deepseek-v4-pro
```

1. Have the gateway running with a valid Codex OAuth session.
2. Let the Codex credentials become unavailable — either the OAuth token gets cleared/expired from `auth.json` (`providers` ends up empty), or simply remove it. (Quota/`usage_limit_reached` does NOT trigger this — creds still resolve, so init succeeds and the in-loop fallback handles it. This bug is specifically the **missing/expired-credential** case.)
3. Start a **new** session (e.g. send a fresh message to the Telegram/Discord bot, or open a new TUI session).

**Expected:** init falls back to `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` (as cron and the CLI do).
**Actual:** `agent init failed: No Codex credentials stored. Run `hermes auth` to authenticate.` — no fallback. Pre-existing sessions continue to fall back normally, which makes it look intermittent.

## Root cause

`_make_agent` in `tui_gateway/server.py` resolves the runtime provider with a bare call:

```python
runtime = resolve_runtime_provider(
    requested=requested_provider,
    target_model=model or None,
)
```

`resolve_runtime_provider("openai-codex")` raises `AuthError` for an **explicitly requested** provider when creds are missing (it only falls through for `requested="auto"`). There is no try/except around this call in `_make_agent`, so the `AuthError` propagates to the gateway build handler and surfaces as `agent init failed: …`.

By contrast, the two other build paths already wrap this and walk the fallback chain:

- `cron/scheduler.py` — `except AuthError:` → iterates `fallback_providers` / `fallback_model`, calling `resolve_runtime_provider(requested=entry["provider"])` for each.
- `hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py` → `CLIAgentSetupMixin._ensure_runtime_credentials` — same pattern over `self._fallback_model` (the normalized list from `get_fallback_chain`).

`agent/agent_init.py` also has an "init-time fallback (#17929)" path, but it only fires when `resolve_provider_client` returns `None`; it's bypassed here because the gateway resolves creds **before** `agent_init` via `resolve_runtime_provider`, which raises.

## Suggested fix

Give `_make_agent` the same init-time fallback the scheduler and CLI have: wrap the `resolve_runtime_provider` call(s), and on `AuthError` walk `get_fallback_chain(_load_cfg())`, switching `model` / `provider` to the first entry that resolves. Re-raise if nothing in the chain resolves so the existing error path still surfaces.

Sketch:

```python
from hermes_cli.auth import AuthError
from hermes_cli.fallback_config import get_fallback_chain

try:
    runtime = resolve_runtime_provider(requested=requested_provider, target_model=model or None)
except AuthError as primary_exc:
    runtime = None
    for entry in get_fallback_chain(_load_cfg()):
        fb_provider, fb_model = entry.get("provider"), entry.get("model")
        if not fb_provider or not fb_model:
            continue
        try:
            runtime = resolve_runtime_provider(requested=fb_provider, target_model=fb_model)
            model, requested_provider = fb_model, fb_provider
            break
        except Exception:
            continue
    if runtime is None:
        raise  # preserve existing "agent init failed: …" behavior
```

I applied essentially this locally (a `_resolve_runtime_with_init_fallback` helper routed through both `resolve_runtime_provider` call sites in `_make_agent`) and confirmed a new session with missing Codex creds now resolves to `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` (`fell_back=True`) instead of erroring.

## Related

- #12058 — adjacent but distinct: that report is about a spurious `No Codex credentials stored` banner being appended in the chat client **while the gateway still produces real responses** (creds present). This issue is the opposite — creds genuinely missing, **new sessions hard-fail at init with no fallback**.

items.title: [Bug]: Hermes Desktop + Open Design MCP — `memory-llm` falls through to OpenAI SDK placeholder key, blocking all runs

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

## Bug Description

When the **Open Design** daemon (an MCP server that drives a child Hermes agent through ACP/JSON-RPC) launches a design run, the child agent's `memory-llm` subsystem makes an outbound HTTPS call to **`https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`** even though the user's configured main provider is `minimax-cn` / `MiniMax-M3` and **no OpenAI key exists anywhere** in the user's environment.

The call fails with HTTP `401 invalid_api_key` and the run is aborted within ~30 s with `errorCode: AGENT_EXECUTION_FAILED`. The leaked key (`sk-proj-…u2wA`, reported by OpenAI in the 401 body) is **not user-supplied** — it looks like an SDK-bundled placeholder / hard-coded fixture that the auxiliary fallback chain stumbles into when it cannot resolve the user's `minimax-cn` provider.

**This blocks every `start_run` from the Open Design integration on a clean install where the user does not use OpenAI.**

### Related issues (same root-cause cluster, please read first)

This bug is part of the **active auxiliary-fallback misroute cluster**:

- #44746 — `auxiliary auto can pair live runtime provider with stale main model`
- #45472 — named `custom:<name>` provider loses identity in auxiliary resolution
- #45480 — auxiliary auto-detect falls through to wrong provider when main is named custom
- #45531 — `_normalize_aux_provider` rewrites `custom:kimi` → `kimi-coding`
- **#45545 — `resolve_runtime_provider(requested="custom")` can't resolve the named custom provider, falls back to OpenRouter** (closest match to mine)
- #45565 — auxiliary/fallback routes requests to wrong provider endpoint
- PR #46923 — open, attempting to keep auto model paired with live runtime

### How this report differs from #45545 / #45565

| | #45545 / #45565 (already filed) | **This report** |
|---|---|---|
| Fallback chain terminus | OpenRouter (rejected) or a misconfigured custom provider | **Direct `api.openai.com` with an SDK-bundled placeholder `sk-proj-…u2wA`** |
| Visible error | OpenRouter rejection or HTTP 400 from wrong-provider | **HTTP 401 from OpenAI** with a key that **does not exist in the user's config** |
| Trigger | Multiple custom providers + named `custom:<name>` main runtime | **Single configured provider (`minimax-cn`)**, no custom providers at all, no named custom main runtime |
| Surface | Vision / compression / title-gen | **`memory-llm` boot path of an ACP-launched child agent** (Open Design integration) |
| Reproducibility | Intermittent | **Deterministic — every run fails** |

In other words: the same chain bug is reaching **one step further down** the fallback ladder in my case. Where #45545 stops at OpenRouter (which `_resolve_custom_runtime` rejects), my run walks past that into a bare `OpenAI(...)` SDK construction with a placeholder key — probably the `os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "")` path in `auxiliary_client.py` step 4 (`Custom endpoint (config.yaml model.base_url + OPENAI_API_KEY)`) being entered with an empty `base_url` and a non-empty placeholder `api_key` from somewhere deeper in the dependency tree.

### Suggested test for the maintainer

If you fix the `_try_custom_endpoint` / `_resolve_custom_runtime` chain in #45545 / #46923, please add a regression case that asserts: **with the user's main provider set to `minimax-cn` (or any non-OpenAI provider) and no `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_BASE_URL` set anywhere, an ACP-launched child agent's `memory-llm` boot must not produce any outbound request to `api.openai.com`.** Today it does, which is the regression I'm reporting.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes Desktop v0.16.0 on Windows.
2. Configure `model.default: MiniMax-M3`, `model.provider: minimax-cn` (only provider configured).
3. Leave `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_BASE_URL` unset in `.env`, `config.yaml`, and Windows User/Machine/Process environment.
4. Start the Open Design daemon (Electron-as-Node, MCP server on `http://127.0.0.1:7456`).
5. From Hermes Desktop, call `mcp_open_design_create_project` → `mcp_open_design_start_run` with a trivial prompt (a one-page dark-themed HTML card was used).
6. Poll `mcp_open_design_get_run`.

Result: within ~30 s the run reports `status: failed`, `errorCode: AGENT_EXECUTION_FAILED`, `error: json-rpc id 2: Internal error`. No artifact is produced (`list_files` → `[]`). The Open Design daemon log at `%LocalAppData%/hermes/logs/od-daemon.log` contains exactly one fatal line — `[memory-llm] openai call failed openai 401`.

### Expected Behavior

Every auxiliary call inside an ACP-launched child Hermes agent — including the `memory-llm` boot path — should resolve the user's **main provider** (`minimax-cn / MiniMax-M3` in this case) as step 1 of the documented chain in `agent/auxiliary_client.py`. The Open Design run should produce a design artifact (`index.html`) and finish in the normal 5–30 min window that `start_run` advertises.

No outbound request to `api.openai.com` should be made unless the user has explicitly configured an OpenAI provider (`OPENAI_BASE_URL` + `OPENAI_API_KEY`) **and** that provider is the one selected by the auxiliary chain for the task at hand. With no OpenAI configuration present, a call to `api.openai.com` is a leak of the fallback chain past its intended terminus.

### Actual Behavior

The MCP/ACP layers all initialise cleanly and the child Hermes agent registers 43 MCP tools successfully (`open-design` × 20 + `playwright-chrome` × 23). The crash happens **after** boot, inside the child agent, when `memory-llm` makes the OpenAI call.

### Daemon log (`%LocalAppData%/hermes/logs/od-daemon.log`)

```
[od] listening on http://127.0.0.1:7456
[memory-llm] openai call failed openai 401: {
  "error": {
    "message": "Incorrect API key provided: sk-proj-********************************************************************************************************************************************************u2wA. You can find your API key at https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "invalid_api_key",
    "param": null
  },
  "status": 401
}
```

### Run envelope returned by `mcp_open_design_get_run`

```json
{
  "status": "failed",
  "exitCode": 1,
  "signal": "SIGTERM",
  "error": "json-rpc id 2: Internal error",
  "errorCode": "AGENT_EXECUTION_FAILED",
  "resumable": false,
  "toolBundle": { "mcpServers": [] }
}
```

`mcp_open_design_list_files` after failure returns `{"files": []}` — no artifact produced.

### Run events log (clean ACP bring-up, fatal only at the tail)

```
[INFO] acp_adapter.entry: Loaded env from C:\Users\BLO\AppData\Local\hermes\.env
[INFO] acp_adapter.entry: Starting hermes-agent ACP adapter
[INFO] tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'open-design' (stdio): registered 20 tool(s)
[INFO] tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'playwright-chrome' (stdio): registered 23 tool(s)
[INFO] tools.mcp_tool:   MCP: 43 tool(s) from 2 server(s)
[INFO] acp_adapter.server: ACP client connected
[INFO] acp_adapter.server: Initialize from open-design (protocol v1)
[INFO] run_agent: Loaded environment variables from C:\Users\BLO\AppData\Local\hermes\.env
[ERROR] root: Background task failed
… acp.exceptions.RequestError: Internal error
[diagnostic] runtime_close  rpc_close_reason=fatal_rpc_error  status=failed
[run_retry_finished] retry_strategy=same_run_transient
                    failure_category=tool_error  failure_stage=tool_execution
                    retry_result=suppressed  retry_suppressed_reason=unsupported_category
```

Note: the internal retry logic already classified this as `tool_error` and chose not to retry — so the inner `memory-llm` call site is hard-fatal, not a transient network blip.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
`hermes debug share` is not directly runnable from my Open Design / MCP path — the failure happens inside an ACP-launched child agent. The relevant logs are local files:

- Daemon log: `%LocalAppData%/hermes/logs/od-daemon.log` (full content reproduced in the **Actual Behavior** section above)
- Per-run events log: `C:\Users\BLO\AppData\Local\Programs\Open Design\resources\app\prebundled\.od\runs\860e486d-bfb8-4d3c-b880-9e0eb91addbf\events.jsonl` (reproduced in **Actual Behavior**)
- Run id (reproducer): `860e486d-bfb8-4d3c-b880-9e0eb91addbf`
- Project id (safe to delete): `smoke-test-001`

If a maintainer wants a fresh debug share I am happy to run `hermes debug share` against the parent Hermes CLI session, but it will not capture the child-agent ACP run unless that path also emits to the same debug stream — which it does not appear to.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11 (24H2), x86_64, MSYS bash for shell, Open Design daemon runs as Electron-as-Node.

### Python Version

3.13.12 (hermes-agent venv ships 3.11.x for the embedded agent; failure is in the embedded Python, not my interactive shell's Python).

### Hermes Version

Hermes Desktop / Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (build 2026.6.5, upstream 5e01a5db). `pyproject.toml` `version = "0.16.0"`, `name = "hermes-agent"`.

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

### Where the call is coming from

The log line `[memory-llm] openai call failed openai 401` is the only fatal line in the daemon log. The string `memory-llm` is **not present** in any source file under `agent/` (searched `agent/**/*.py`, excluding `venv/`, `__pycache__/`). The most likely sources are:

1. `agent/auxiliary_client.py` step 4 ("Custom endpoint — `config.yaml model.base_url + OPENAI_API_KEY`", lines ~1815–1845). That branch returns `None, None, None` when `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is unset, so it **should not** produce the call — but a downstream consumer may still reach this branch with non-empty inputs.
2. A vendored / bundled module that constructs an `openai.OpenAI(...)` client using a non-empty placeholder key when neither `OPENAI_BASE_URL` nor a real key is configured.

The trailing characters of the leaked key (`…u2wA`) match the shape of OpenAI documentation fixture keys, suggesting an SDK-bundled default.

### Why the user-config chain does not catch this

`agent/auxiliary_client.py` lines 1–60 (docstring) documents the resolution order:

1. User's main provider + main model (regardless of provider type)
2. OpenRouter
3. Nous Portal
4. Custom endpoint (`config.yaml model.base_url + OPENAI_API_KEY`)
5. Native Anthropic
6. Direct API-key providers (z.ai/GLM, Kimi/Moonshot, MiniMax, MiniMax-CN)
7. None

The user's `model.provider` is `minimax-cn` with a working credential in `auth.json`. Step 1 should hit. But step 4 explicitly reads `os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")` (line ~1824 of the file), and `os.getenv` returns the empty string `""` by default — so the only way a non-empty `sk-proj-…u2wA` key is observed at the call site is if it was injected **after** `os.getenv` (e.g. a vendored `openai` SDK initialising a `default_api_key` from an internal fixture, or a config layer that defaults missing keys to a placeholder).

### Clean-config proof (so reviewers do not second-guess "just unset your key")

All four standard credential locations were inspected:

- `~/.hermes/.env` — no `OPENAI_API_KEY`; only `MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY`, `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY`, `FAL_KEY`, `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, `ZOTERO_API_KEY`
- `~/.hermes/config.yaml` — `openai:` block exists with `api_key: ''`, `base_url: ''`
- Windows User / Machine / Process env — `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset in all three layers (verified via `[System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('OPENAI_API_KEY', scope)`)
- `~/.hermes/auth.json` — `active_provider: null`; only `credential_pool.minimax-cn` populated, no `openai` entry

The leaked key `sk-proj-…u2wA` is therefore not user-supplied.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

### Direction (PR-able, not a patch)

Two layers need to change:

1. **Stop the auxiliary fallback chain at the user's main runtime** for any task that did not explicitly request a different provider. PR #46923 already targets this for the auto-provider pairing; my report asks for the same fix to be extended to:
   - The `memory-llm` boot path specifically (it appears to bypass `_resolve_auto` entirely).
   - The fallback chain when only the **first custom provider** in `config.yaml` is encountered — `_try_custom_endpoint` should not silently fall through to a bare `OpenAI(...)` construction.

2. **Defence in depth: refuse to construct an OpenAI client with an unverified key when the user has not configured one.** A small validator at the SDK construction site (or in `auxiliary_client._resolve_custom_runtime`) that rejects `api_key` values matching the OpenAI documentation's fixture patterns (`sk-proj-…u2wA`, `sk-…abc…`, etc.) would have caught this without the chain rewrite.

### Specific regression test to add

```python
def test_memory_llm_does_not_call_openai_when_user_uses_non_openai_provider(monkeypatch):
    # Simulate a clean install: only minimax-cn configured, no OPENAI_API_KEY.
    monkeypatch.delenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", raising=False)

    seen_calls = []
    class _TrapOpenAI:
        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            seen_calls.append(("constructed", args, kwargs))
        class chat:  # noqa: E701 — minimal stub
            class completions:
                @staticmethod
                def create(**_): raise AssertionError("memory-llm called api.openai.com")

    monkeypatch.setattr("openai.OpenAI", _TrapOpenAI)
    # ... boot the child agent the way Open Design does ...
    assert seen_calls == [], f"unexpected OpenAI client construction: {seen_calls}"
```

This test would have failed loudly on v0.16.0 and would catch any future regression of the same shape.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: hermes curator restore can restore the wrong skill and delete an unrelated archived one

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
**Affected Component:** Skills (skill loading, hub, guard)

> Scope note: this is the `restore` path over the per-skill `.archive/` directories in `tools/skill_usage.py`. It is a different bug from #47612, which is the `rollback` path over the tar.gz snapshots in `.curator_backups/` (`agent/curator_backup.py`). The two share no code.

### What happened
When I run `hermes curator restore <name>` for a skill that is not in the archive under that exact name, the restore can match a different archived skill whose directory name starts with `<name>-`, move that skill out of `.archive/` into `~/.hermes/skills/<name>`, and report success. The skill I asked for is not restored, and the unrelated skill I actually had archived is gone from the archive.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Have an agent-created skill whose name is a prefix of another, for example `git-helpers` (the same thing happens with `apple-notes` vs `apple`, or `github-issues` vs `github`).
2. Archive it with `hermes curator archive git-helpers`, or let the curator archive it for inactivity. It lands at `~/.hermes/skills/.archive/git-helpers/`.
3. There is no archived skill named exactly `git`.
4. Run `hermes curator restore git`.
5. The command prints `restored to .../skills/git` and exits 0, but what it did was move `git-helpers` out of the archive and rename it to `git`. `hermes curator list-archived` no longer shows `git-helpers`, and `~/.hermes/skills/git/SKILL.md` still says `name: git-helpers` inside.

### Expected
Restoring a name that is not in the archive should fail with "not found in archive" and leave every archived skill untouched. The only non-exact match that should ever count is the timestamped duplicate `archive_skill` itself writes on a name collision (`<skill>-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`).

### Actual
The restore matches any archived directory whose name starts with `<name>-`, so it pulls an unrelated sibling skill out of the archive, renames it, and reports success.

### Root cause (from reading the code)
In `tools/skill_usage.py`, `restore_skill()` first looks for an archive directory whose name equals the requested skill, then falls back to `p.name.startswith(f"{skill_name}-")`. That fallback is meant to catch the timestamped duplicate `archive_skill()` creates on a collision (it appends `datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')`, a 14 digit suffix). But `startswith("<name>-")` also matches any other archived skill named `<name>-something`, so a sibling like `git-helpers` is treated as a duplicate of `git`.

### Impact
This is a recovery path that silently destroys data. The skill I asked to restore is not restored, and a different archived skill is taken out of `.archive/` and left on disk under a directory name that no longer matches its frontmatter `name:`. The restore reports success, so there is no signal that the wrong skill moved or that the archived sibling is gone.

### Debug Report
Reproduced from a clean checkout of `main` at 5e01a5d two independent ways. A function-level pytest regression (in the linked pull request), and end to end at the command line:

```
$ hermes curator archive git-helpers
curator: archived to ~/.hermes/skills/.archive/git-helpers
$ hermes curator archive git-flow-notes
curator: archived to ~/.hermes/skills/.archive/git-flow-notes
$ hermes curator list-archived
git-flow-notes
git-helpers
$ hermes curator restore git          # no skill named 'git' was ever archived
curator: restored to ~/.hermes/skills/git
$ hermes curator list-archived
git-flow-notes                        # git-helpers is gone
```

After that restore, `~/.hermes/skills/git/SKILL.md` still reads `name: git-helpers`, and `~/.hermes/skills/.archive/git-helpers` no longer exists. With the fix, the same `hermes curator restore git` prints `skill 'git' not found in archive` (exit 1) and leaves both archived skills in place.

### Environment
Reproduced from a clean checkout of `main` at commit 5e01a5d. It is pure string and path logic on directory names with default config, so it shows up on every operating system.

items.title: Feature request: Perseus context engine as first-class live context provider

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Summary

Proposal: integrate [Perseus](https://github.com/tcconnally/perseus) as a live context resolution engine for Hermes agents.

## What Perseus is

Perseus is an open-source (MIT) live context engine for AI agents. Instead of baking static instructions into prompts, Perseus resolves directives at inference time: `@file`, `@memory`, `@search`, `@query`, `@agent`, `@tool`, `@skills`, and 20+ more. It pulls in workspace files, project memory (Mneme), git state, MCP tool output, and service health — all fresh on every call.

- **17K+ downloads/month** on PyPI (`pip install perseus`)
- **MIT licensed**, pure Python
- **MCP-native** — `perseus mcp serve` exposes directives as callable tools
- **Hermes already references it** — `context.engine: perseus` exists in config.yaml

## Where it fits

Hermes already has the `context.engine: perseus` config key. This proposal makes it a documented, polished integration:

1. **Auto-resolve AGENTS.md at session start** — when `context.engine: perseus`, Hermes resolves `@file AGENTS.md` as part of system prompt assembly
2. **Perseus MCP tools** — register Perseus directives as MCP tools when the server is configured
3. **Mneme memory bridge** — Perseus's narrative project memory could complement Hermes's memory system

## What's already built

- A `perseus-context` skill that teaches Hermes agents Perseus directive syntax
- [hermes-mimir](https://github.com/tcconnally/hermes-mimir) memory provider plugin (separate but complementary)

Happy to contribute the skill, docs, and any code changes needed.

items.title: Bug: Mac Telegram Rich Messages render CJK characters as garbled overlapping symbols
items.body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes sends responses via Bot API 10.1 Rich Messages (`sendRichMessage` / `sendRichMessageDraft`), the **Mac Telegram client** renders **CJK characters** (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) as garbled overlapping symbols — appearing as a cluster of misaligned character fragments near the message bubble. 

The **final message bubble content is correct**, but a garbled draft/overlay artifact remains visible, cluttering the UI.

This affects **every message** containing CJK text, not just single characters. iOS may be affected too (unconfirmed).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Hermes gateway on Telegram with Rich Messages enabled (Bot API 10.1, current `main`)
2. Send any message that produces a CJK response (e.g., "早" or "看看我的持仓")
3. Observe the Mac Telegram client — CJK text shows garbled overlapping symbol clusters

## Expected Behavior

CJK characters should render cleanly in Rich Message drafts and final messages, same as the legacy MarkdownV2 path.

## Actual Behavior

Garbled overlapping CJK glyphs appear as draft overlay artifacts. Screenshot available if needed.

## Environment

- **Platform**: macOS Telegram client
- **Hermes**: current `main` (post Rich Messages merge)
- **Bot API**: 10.1 (`sendRichMessage` / `sendRichMessageDraft`)

## Workaround

Disabling Rich Messages entirely (making `_should_attempt_rich` return `False`) and falling back to legacy `sendMessage` + MarkdownV2 fixes the rendering. This confirms the bug is in the Rich Message render path, not in general CJK handling.

## Related Issues

- #45911 — Inconsistent message rendering on Mac/iOS post-Rich Messages
- #45762 — Rich Message body text renders oversized

## Proposed Fix

Two options:
1. **(Hermes side)** Add a config option to disable Rich Messages per-platform or globally, so users on affected clients can opt out without code changes.
2. **(Telegram side)** Fix the Mac client Rich Message renderer for CJK characters — but this is outside Hermes control.

items.title: Z.AI GLM-5.2 Coding Plan returns 429/code 1305 when system prompt contains exact phrase "Hermes Agent"

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

Z.AI / GLM Coding Plan (`glm-5.2` on `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`) returns a misleading HTTP 429 / provider code `1305` when the **system prompt contains the exact phrase `Hermes Agent`**.

This looks different from normal provider overload: the same key, endpoint, model, request shape, and prompt length work after replacing only that phrase, e.g. `Hermes Agent` -> `Hermes framework`.

Related but not identical to existing overload/classification/provider-split work:

- #14038
- #15297
- #15414
- #47140
- #47205

Those discuss overload handling / Coding Plan provider routing. This issue is specifically about a prompt-sensitive false 429 trigger.

## Environment

- Provider: `zai`
- Model: `glm-5.2`
- Base URL: `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`
- SDK path: OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions
- Auth: API key redacted

## Minimal reproduction

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="REDACTED",
    base_url="https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4",
)

# Fails with HTTP 429 / code 1305
client.chat.completions.create(
    model="glm-5.2",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "Hermes Agent"},
        {"role": "user", "content": "只回复 OK"},
    ],
    stream=True,
    max_tokens=16,
)

# Works: same key, same endpoint, same model, only the system phrase changed
client.chat.completions.create(
    model="glm-5.2",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "Hermes framework"},
        {"role": "user", "content": "只回复 OK"},
    ],
    stream=True,
    max_tokens=16,
)
```

## Observed error

```text
Error code: 429 - {'error': {'code': '1305', 'message': 'The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later'}}
```

## Additional local verification

In a Hermes profile configured for `zai/glm-5.2` Coding Plan, requests repeatedly failed with:

```text
HTTP 429: The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later
provider=zai model=glm-5.2 base_url=https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4
```

After replacing every effective-system-prompt occurrence of the exact phrase `Hermes Agent` with `Hermes framework`, the same session/request succeeded:

```text
API call #1: model=glm-5.2 provider=zai in=11261 out=3 total=11264 latency=3.8s
```

A fresh Telegram gateway session also succeeded after sanitizing all prompt sources and restarting the gateway:

```text
API call #1: model=glm-5.2 provider=zai in=35746 out=28 total=35774 latency=11.0s
```

## Why this matters

Hermes can include the exact phrase `Hermes Agent` from multiple effective system prompt sources, not just one constant:

- runtime/help guidance
- skill mandatory guidance
- skill descriptions / skills index
- context files
- persisted `state.db.sessions.system_prompt` for resumed sessions

So a one-line replacement in one prompt constant is not enough. New and resumed sessions can still hit the prompt-sensitive 429 if any remaining prompt source contains the exact phrase.

## Possible fix / mitigation

For Z.AI / GLM Coding Plan requests, sanitize the effective system prompt before sending:

```python
system_prompt = system_prompt.replace("Hermes Agent", "Hermes framework")
```

This should probably happen late in system prompt assembly so it covers skill descriptions, context files, and generated skill indexes as well as static prompt constants.

A narrower provider-gated mitigation may be preferable if we do not want to alter prompts for all providers.
