- Kanban CLI: `hermes kanban init`, `hermes kanban create`, etc.
- Dashboard Kanban: accessible via `hermes dashboard` command

items.title: Mid-session model switch leaves stale Model/Provider in persisted system prompt

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

After switching a gateway session's model mid-conversation, the runtime can call the new provider/model successfully, but the Web UI/session metadata may continue to show an old model such as `gpt-5.5`.

The stale label comes from `sessions.system_prompt`: `switch_model()` only clears `agent._cached_system_prompt` in memory. Gateway turns construct fresh `AIAgent` instances and restore the persisted `sessions.system_prompt` for prefix-cache stability, so the next turn can resurrect a stale `Model:` / `Provider:` header from SQLite.

## Observed behavior

Real local example from `state.db` before patching:

```text
sessions.model:            glm-5.2
sessions.billing_provider: openai-codex
sessions.system_prompt:    ...
Model: gpt-5.5
Provider: openai-codex
...
```

In another switch, provider logs confirmed calls to `xiaomi/mimo-v2.5`, while the Web UI displayed the stale `gpt-5.5` tag.

## Expected behavior

A successful mid-session model switch should invalidate any persisted system prompt snapshot that embeds the old volatile `Model:` / `Provider:` header, so the next turn rebuilds it from the active runtime/session state.

## Root cause

`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py::switch_model()` does:

```python
agent._cached_system_prompt = None
```

but it does not invalidate the SQLite `sessions.system_prompt` snapshot. Later, gateway/conversation restoration can reuse that persisted prompt.

`hermes_state.py::update_session_model()` currently updates only the `model` column:

```sql
UPDATE sessions SET model = ? WHERE id = ?
```

## Suggested fix

Make the persisted model switch also clear `system_prompt`, and have `switch_model()` call it fail-open after clearing the in-memory cache:

```sql
UPDATE sessions SET model = ?, system_prompt = NULL WHERE id = ?
```

This preserves the existing dashboard/session-model fix while forcing the cached prompt to be rebuilt with the new `Model:` / `Provider:` values.

I applied this locally and added/updated a regression assertion that `update_session_model()` nulls `system_prompt`.

## Local verification

```text
PYTHONPATH=/opt/hermes uv run --no-project --with pytest python -m pytest /opt/hermes/tests/test_hermes_state.py -q -o 'addopts=' -k update_session_model
# 1 passed, 261 deselected
```

Also verified with a direct `SessionDB` smoke test:

```text
model= xiaomi/mimo-v2.5
system_prompt= None
```

items.title: [Bug]: OAuth Pro/Max/Team requests rejected with HTTP 400 "third-party / extra usage" (missing x-anthropic-billing-header system block)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description
With a Claude Pro/Max/Team OAuth credential (`sk-ant-oat01-*`) on the `anthropic` provider, requests are currently rejected with:

```
HTTP 400 invalid_request_error:
"Third-party apps now draw from extra usage, not plan limits.
 Ask your workspace admin to add more and keep going."
```

This makes Pro/Max/Team OAuth effectively unusable on-plan.

This previously worked. Per Anthropic's help article ["Use the Claude Agent SDK with your Claude plan"](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15036540-use-the-claude-agent-sdk-with-your-claude-plan), a ~June 15 2026 change that would meter programmatic usage was **paused** ("…still draw from your subscription's usage limits"). Empirically the pause only restores on-plan billing for traffic that presents as the genuine Agent-SDK/CLI surface — i.e. requests that carry the `x-anthropic-billing-header … cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli` system block. Hermes omits that block, so it is, for now, treated as third-party traffic.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Add a Claude Pro/Max/Team OAuth credential: `hermes auth add anthropic` (or paste an `sk-ant-oat01-*` token).
2. Run a request:
   ```
   hermes -z "say hi" -m claude-opus-4-8 --provider anthropic --cli
   ```
3. The request returns HTTP 400 "...extra usage, not plan limits".

## Expected Behavior
The OAuth request should return HTTP 200 with `usage.service_tier: "standard"`, drawn from the subscription plan — the same as the genuine `claude` CLI on the same account (`apiProvider: firstParty`).

## Actual Behavior
```
HTTP 400 invalid_request_error
"Third-party apps now draw from extra usage, not plan limits.
 Ask your workspace admin to add more and keep going."
```
A/B on a live Team plan:

| `system[0]` billing block | result |
|---|---|
| absent (current) | **HTTP 400** |
| `cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli` present | **HTTP 200** (plan) |

## Affected Component
Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory) — specifically the Anthropic OAuth request path in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py`.

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)
N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report
```shell
--- hermes dump ---
version:   0.16.0 (2026.6.5)
os:        Darwin 25.5.0 arm64
python:    3.11.15
model:     claude-opus-4-8
provider:  anthropic

--- agent.log (relevant lines, secrets redacted) ---
agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 400 -
  {'type':'error','error':{'type':'invalid_request_error','message':'Third-party apps now
  draw from extra usage, not plan limits. Ask your workspace admin to add more and keep
  going.'}, 'request_id':'req_011Cc9nVo4Ca6j3FzBuFpJTK'}
agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=BadRequestError
  provider=anthropic base_url=https://api.anthropic.com model=claude-opus-4-8
  summary=HTTP 400: Third-party apps now draw from extra usage, not plan limits.
agent.conversation_loop: Non-retryable client error (HTTP 400).
```

## Operating System
macOS 26.5.1 (build 25F80)

## Python Version
3.11.15

## Hermes Version
v0.16.0 (2026.6.5); also reproduced against current `main` (fcf6cb3d7)

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)
Captured from a genuine `claude -p` request to `api.anthropic.com` (HTTP 200) via a local logging proxy (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`). The first system block is a machine-parsed billing-attribution token, distinct from the natural-language identity line:

```
system[0]  x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=2.1.181.d08; cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli;
system[1]  You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.
User-Agent claude-cli/2.1.181 (external, sdk-cli)
x-app      cli
URL        /v1/messages?beta=true
```

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)
The detection is server-side billing/attribution analysis. The genuine Claude Code / Agent-SDK CLI puts the `x-anthropic-billing-header` token as `system[0]`:

```
x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=<version>; cc_entrypoint=<entrypoint>;
```

The OAuth (`is_oauth`) path in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` already declares the Claude Code identity in natural language via `cc_block` ("You are Claude Code…") but **omits `system[0]` (the billing token)**, so requests are attributed as a generic third-party app → extra-usage lane → 400.

What the block contains: `cc_version` (genuine, from the installed `claude` version) and a hardcoded `cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli` label. The captured request carried only these two fields; the gate routes on the `cc_entrypoint` label for this surface.

## Proposed Fix (optional)
Prepend the `x-anthropic-billing-header` block as `system[0]` on the OAuth path in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py`, ahead of the identity prefix — establishing at the billing-attribution layer the same Claude Code identity `cc_block` only asserts in prose. PR attached.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?
- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

## Related
- #32243 (canonical: OAuth Pro/Max → 400)
- #33462 (alternative: register `claude-code` as a subprocess provider)

items.title: [Bug]: 桌面版 Profile 切换后会话列表不显示 / 会话数据跨 Profile 分散

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

环境信息：

Hermes Desktop (Electron 桌面应用)

Windows 10

使用 photo-selectorprofile

Yuanbao 平台绑定到此 profile

问题描述：

在 Hermes 桌面版中，当切换到 photo-selectorprofile 时，看不到在当前 profile 下的聊天记录（比如元宝上的对话）。但这些记录实际上存在正确的 state.db里。

深入分析后发现两个问题：

问题 1：桌面版没有正确设置 active-profile

桌面版启动时从 app.getPath('userData')/active-profile.json读取 profile 设置。这个文件不存在，所以桌面版默认以 defaultprofile 启动。即使用户在侧边栏手动切换到 photo-selector，也可能存在会话列表不能正确刷新的问题。

问题 2：会话数据分散在两个 state.db 中（更严重）

数据分布如下：

时间 | 数据库 | Profile
-- | -- | --
6月11-12日 | %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\state.db | default
6月13日 | %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\profiles\photo-selector\state.db | photo-selector
6月17日 18:27 | photo-selector的 db | photo-selector
6月17日 18:29 | default的 db | ← 又跳回 default！​
6月18日 | photo-selector的 db | photo-selector



### Steps to Reproduce

在 Hermes Desktop 桌面版中使用某个命名 profile

通过 gateway 从消息平台（Yuanbao）发送消息

在桌面版切换 profile

观察会话列表是否完整对应

### Expected Behavior

当 gateway 绑定到 photo-selectorprofile 时，该 profile 的所有会话应该统一在​ photo-selector的 state.db中

切换到 photo-selectorprofile 时，应该能看到所有属于该 profile 的会话

### Actual Behavior

会话数据散落在 default 和 photo-selector 两个 state.db文件中

用户在一个 profile 下看到的会话不完整

桌面版 profile 切换后会话列表未必能正确刷新

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/ybeZY
  gateway.log  https://dpaste.com/6SV6FVTLY
  desktop.log  https://dpaste.com/5W7C7NHU2
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

Hermes Desktop 0.16.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Yuanbao gateway 在启动时没有传 --profile参数（gateway_state.json的 argv 中只有 ["main.py", "gateway", "run"]），因此它只依赖于 HERMES_HOME环境变量。如果用户在不同时刻用不同的 HERMES_HOME启动 gateway，同一个 Yuanbao 账号的会话会被分散到不同的 state.db中。

### Proposed Fix (optional)

桌面版 Electron main process 在启动时应该确保 active-profile.json被正确创建和读取

Gateway 启动时应该带上 --profile参数，确保 HERMES_HOME被正确设置到该 profile 的目录

当用户切换 profile 后，会话列表应该通过 queryClient.invalidateQueries()强制刷新

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: `nousresearch/hermes-agent` Docker image ships `/opt/hermes` as `555 root:root` with no LICENSE file — breaks multi-container Hermes WebUI installs
items.body:
## Summary

The `:latest` Docker image ships `/opt/hermes` as mode `555 root:root` (read-only, owned by root) and **does not include a `LICENSE` file** at the root of `/opt/hermes`. This breaks the documented multi-container Hermes WebUI deployment, where the WebUI container runs `uv pip install /opt/hermes[all]` against a shared volume of the agent source. setuptools cannot create `hermes_agent.egg-info/` next to the package because the directory is unwritable for the WebUI runtime user, and PEP 639's `license-files = ["LICENSE"]` resolves to "Pattern 'LICENSE' did not match any files." WebUI dies under `set -e` before reaching `/health`.

This is observable on `docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` today (2026-06-18, image created the same day).

## Environment

- Image: `docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` (pulled 2026-06-18)
- WebUI: `ghcr.io/nesquena/hermes-webui:latest` (any tag with the staging block from 70f371c8 / v0.51.87+, but the same bug fires on v0.51.83 too — no staging path needed)
- Hermes Agent source version: 0.16.0 (from `pyproject.toml` shipped in the image)
- Deployment: podman / docker compose with shared named volume between hermes-agent and hermes-webui at `/opt/hermes`

## Reproduction

```bash
podman pull docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
podman run --rm --entrypoint '["stat","-c","%a %U:%G %n"]' \
    docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest \
    /opt/hermes /opt/hermes/pyproject.toml /opt/hermes/LICENSE
```

Observed output:

```
555 root:root /opt/hermes
444 root:root /opt/hermes/pyproject.toml
stat: cannot statx '/opt/hermes/LICENSE': No such file or directory
```

And:

```bash
podman run --rm --entrypoint '["ls","-la","/opt/hermes"]' \
    docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest | head -20
```

Shows the top-level files (`.dockerignore`, `Dockerfile`, `MANIFEST.in`, `pyproject.toml`, `batch_runner.py`, `cli.py`, …) are all `-r--r--r-- root root` — no LICENSE entry in the listing.

Then start a multi-container stack (e.g. `docker-compose.two-container.yml` from `nesquena/hermes-webui`) with the shared `hermes-agent-src` volume, point both services at `/opt/hermes`, and bring the WebUI up. The init script runs:

```
uv pip install /opt/hermes[all]
```

…which fails with:

```
[stderr]
running egg_info
creating hermes_agent.egg-info
error: could not create 'hermes_agent.egg-info': Permission denied

[stderr]
/…/site-packages/setuptools/dist.py:483:
SetuptoolsDeprecationWarning: Cannot find any files for the given pattern.

      ********************************************************************************
              Pattern 'LICENSE' did not match any files.
      ********************************************************************************
```

The WebUI container then exits with `!! ERROR: Failed to install hermes-agent's requirements` and never serves traffic.

## Expected

Either:
- `/opt/hermes` is mode `755 root:root` (or similar) so the WebUI runtime user (UID 1000 in the canonical compose, or whatever the operator configures) can write `<pkg>.egg-info/` and `build/` directly under it — matching how a normal sdist checkout looks on disk.
- OR the image provides a documented "shared with hermes-webui" path that doesn't require hermes-webui to write into the agent source.

And `LICENSE` is shipped at the root of `/opt/hermes` so PEP 639 setuptools doesn't emit the deprecation warning (or better yet, until 2027-02-18 doesn't fail).

## Actual

`/opt/hermes` is mode `555 root:root` — hermeswebui (UID 1000) cannot create `<pkg>.egg-info/` inside it. PEP 639 emits a deprecation warning about missing `LICENSE`. WebUI init fails under `set -e`, container exits.

## Why this matters

The `nesquena/hermes-webui` project's documented multi-container compose pattern (`docker-compose.two-container.yml`, `docker-compose.three-container.yml`) **explicitly shares** `/opt/hermes` between the agent and WebUI containers, and the WebUI's `docker_init.bash` runs `uv pip install /opt/hermes[all]` against that shared mount as a normal install path. With the current agent image perms, every multi-container deployment of Hermes WebUI dies at startup.

The hermes-webui maintainers' recent work (`70f371c8`, #2490) added a staging-to-`/tmp` block to dodge a related EROFS class of bug, but the underlying perm issue is in this image, not in the WebUI. The staging chmod workaround on the WebUI side does not fix this for v0.51.83 (no staging path), and even with staging + chmod on a newer WebUI tag, hermeswebui is not the owner of the source tree so a `chmod u+w` on the staged copy in `/tmp` would only paper over the symptom if hermeswebui happens to own the staged files (which it does, but for a non-obvious reason and not reliably across mounts).

## Root cause (in this image)

The Dockerfile builds the `/opt/hermes` directory read-only — `COPY --chmod=555` or equivalent, or it never relaxes the default `COPY` perms for top-level files. The PyPI sdist has `LICENSE` at the root of `hermes-agent/`, but the Docker build context excludes it (`.dockerignore` likely has `LICENSE`, or the `COPY` step doesn't grab it).

I'd expect the image's role to be "pre-extracted agent source, ready for the WebUI to pip-install", and currently it ships as a sealed snapshot nobody can write to. Two complementary fixes:

1. **Make `/opt/hermes` writable for the WebUI runtime user.** Either:
   - Set the dir to `755 root:root` (everyone can read+execute; hermeswebui's write attempts still fail because hermeswebui isn't root — but they only need to write to the top-level dir to create `<pkg>.egg-info/`, and `chmod 777` would let that succeed; `chmod 1777` (sticky) might be the right answer if you want to prevent other users from deleting other users' egg-infos), OR
   - Build `/opt/hermes` to be owned by a configurable build-time UID/GID and set that to the canonical `1000:1000` that hermes-webui runs as, OR
   - Run `chmod -R u+w,g+w /opt/hermes` after the COPY in the Dockerfile (gives owner-write and group-write so the WebUI's UID 1000 in the `users` group can write — which is what the canonical webui Dockerfile creates).

2. **Ship `LICENSE` in the image.** It's already in the sdist and in the upstream git repo. Add it to the Dockerfile `COPY` (or remove it from `.dockerignore`) so `pyproject.toml`'s `license-files = ["LICENSE"]` resolves. This also future-proofs PEP 639 enforcement after 2027-02-18.

Either fix alone unblocks hermes-webui multi-container deployments; both together match what a normal sdist checkout looks like and are the right shape.

## Suggested fix (proposal, not a PR)

In the hermes-agent `Dockerfile`, after the `COPY` that lays down `/opt/hermes`, add:

```dockerfile
# /opt/hermes is consumed by hermes-webui in the canonical two-container
# compose, where the webui runtime user (UID 1000) pip-installs the agent
# from a shared volume. The webui needs to write <pkg>.egg-info/ next to the
# package, so the source tree must be writable by that user. Ship LICENSE
# too so PEP 639 license-files resolution doesn't warn or (post 2027-02-18)
# fail.
RUN chmod -R a+rwX /opt/hermes \
 && cp /opt/hermes/LICENSE /opt/hermes/LICENSE 2>/dev/null || true
```

(That `cp` is a no-op if LICENSE is already there — adjust if the agent source genuinely doesn't ship one.)

If you'd prefer a tighter perms model (e.g. ship `0755 root:root` plus a build-time `groupadd -g 1000 hermeswebui && chgrp -R 1000 /opt/hermes`), that's also fine — just make sure the WebUI runtime user can write.

## Related

- `nesquena/hermes-webui#4395` / PR #4398 — workaround on the WebUI side that papers over the perm-inheritance variant of this same class (still useful, but not the fix).
- `nesquena/hermes-webui#23402` (closed, marked `sweeper:implemented-on-main`) — a related Docker permissions issue; that report included a `ls -la /opt/hermes` showing mixed `10000:10000` and `root` ownership. Current `:latest` has tightened further to uniform `555 root:root`, so even the workaround that report used may no longer apply.
- `nesquena/hermes-webui#17144`, `NousResearch/hermes-agent#10270`, `#29660` — other container-permissions reports, mostly about state files under `$HERMES_HOME` rather than the agent source tree.

## Environment for the report

- `hermes-agent` image: `docker.io/nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` (digest `a1bab27d5b4c8c669e22091ee8c88f2ed21e122bd2204b719d8e8b0968fd3be7`, created 2026-06-18)
- `pyproject.toml` inside image: `name = "hermes-agent"`, `version = "0.16.0"`
- Verification: `podman run --rm` against the image, no special mount needed.

items.title: hermes update --yes wiped entire ~/.hermes/ directory (.env, MEMORY.md, kanban.db, skills, scripts — all gone)

labels.name: P0

items.body:
## Environment
- Hermes Agent: v0.16.0 (2026.6.5), commit `c6b0eb4d` (before incident)

    backup_keep: 5

Symptom
The entire ~/.hermes/ directory was wiped after hermes update --yes ran via a cron job. Everything lost:

- kanban.db (action items)

- scripts/ (calendar-sync.py, pluggy-sync.py, weekly-review.sh, etc.)
- config.yaml, gateway_state.json, logs/
Only ~/.local/bin/hermes (117-byte wrapper) and the systemd service unit survived.
Reproduction (partial — exact pane logs lost)
1. Internal Hermes cron job (0 6 */3 * *) triggers hermes-self-update.sh
2. Script uses setsid nohup to detach a worker (no timeout) running hermes update --yes
3. The dispatcher returns in <120s (logs worker: start + worker pre:) and Hermes marks the job last_status: ok
4. The detached worker runs hermes update --yes for 37+ hours (Jun 16 06:00 → Jun 17 19:37) without ever logging worker update rc=, worker post:, or sending failure/success report
5. At some point during those 37h, ~/.hermes/ was completely deleted
Evidence of stuck worker
Log ~/.local/state/hermes-self-update.log — 4 consecutive runs (Jun 10, 13, 16, 17) all show the same pattern:
2026-06-16T06:00:47Z update disponivel -- disparando worker destacado
2026-06-16T06:00:47Z worker: start
2026-06-16T06:00:52Z worker pre: sha=a8562761243fa51dc0f5f7e982049bbc9ef0fed6 ver=Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream c6b0eb4d
# <end of log — never reached "worker update rc=" or "worker post:">
So hermes update --yes started, captured OLD_SHA/OLD_VER, called "$HERMES_BIN" update --yes 2>&1 — and never returned.
Destructive steps in hermes update flow (hermes_cli/main.py:_cmd_update_impl)
The handler executes, in sequence, multiple operations that can delete files if interrupted mid-flight:
1. _run_pre_update_backup (main.py:7984) — skipped because pre_update_backup: false (default). No safety net.
2. git reset --hard origin/main if git pull --ff-only fails (diverged history). Only affects ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/, but...
3. _clear_bytecode_cache — removes __pycache__
4. uv pip install -e ".[all]" — reinstalls deps in venv
5. sync_skills (tools/skills_sync.py) — MULTIPLE _rmtree_writable calls (lines 595, 605, 615, 750, 894). If dest is computed wrong or the process is killed mid shutil.move + shutil.copytree, skills can be lost.
6. seed_profile_skills for all profiles
7. backfill_profile_envs — copies .env between profiles
8. Gateway restart
Root cause hypothesis
Without exact pane logs (lost because we restored a snapshot from Jun 16 18:13, before the Jun 17 19:37 pane), the exact step cannot be pinpointed. Strongest hypotheses:
1. hermes update --yes hung (likely: uv pip install waiting on network, or sync_skills in deadlock, or git pull stash conflict) for 37h.
2. The process was eventually killed (system OOM? cascading SIGTERM from systemd user session restart? git timeout?) mid destructive step — possibly during sync_skills or git reset --hard.
3. Without pre_update_backup, there was no recovery zip. The create_quick_snapshot(label="pre-update", keep=1) (main.py:~8700) is belt-and-suspenders, but if the wipe happened AFTER the snapshot and the snapshot itself was lost...
Verification: bug still present in latest main (commit 3769dff5, Jun 18 2026)
I updated manually (interactive TTY, no --yes) to 3769dff5 (142 commits past the incident). Checked the changelog and current code:
- pre_update_backup still defaults to false (main.py:8117). No commit touched _run_pre_update_backup or its default.
- skills_sync.py unchanged — same 5 _rmtree_writable calls (lines 595, 605, 615, 750, 894), no scope guard added. _rmtree_writable(path) still does shutil.rmtree(path) without validating path is inside HERMES_HOME/skills/.
- None of the 142 commits mention skills_sync, rmtree, pre_update_backup, or the wipe incident.
- hermes update --yes still has no timeout — can hang 37h again.
Recommendations
1. updates.pre_update_backup should default to true (or at least on --yes/non-interactive runs). Cost of a few minutes of zip is negligible vs. total loss of .env + MEMORY.md + kanban.db.
2. hermes update --yes needs a timeout — a process hung 37h unsupervised is dangerous. Suggest --timeout flag or sensible default (e.g. 10 min).
3. Post-update guard rails: before declaring success, validate critical HERMES_HOME files still exist (.env, config.yaml, MEMORY.md if present before). If any disappeared during update, abort and restore from backup/snapshot.
4. sync_skills should not use _rmtree_writable on paths that can escape ~/.hermes/skills/ — add assertion that dest is inside HERMES_HOME/skills/ before any rmtree.
5. The setsid nohup <worker> pattern without supervision (common in user cron scripts) is fragile. Document in hermes update warning that it's not safe for long unsupervised non-interactive runs without external timeout.
6. _rmtree_writable in skills_sync.py:665 uses shutil.rmtree(path, onerror=_on_error) with retry — if path is erroneously ~/.hermes/ (not ~/.hermes/skills/<name>), it wipes everything. Add scope guard.
Workaround applied
- Self-update script renamed to .disabled
- Cron job 891eb5cf4186 kept as paused in jobs.json
- Lock file removed
- Updates now run only manually via hermes update (with TTY, no --yes)
Recovery
Hetzner server snapshot (from Jun 16 18:13 UTC, before the Jun 17 19:37 pane). Restored successfully — ~/.hermes/ complete, gateway healthy.
---
Happy to provide any additional logs or test a fix branch. The worker pre: / worker post: log pattern from hermes-self-update.log (4 stuck runs) should be reproducible if you want me to run diagnostics on a non-production VPS.

items.title: feat: Add Neuralwatt as a native LLM provider

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Feature Description

Add **Neuralwatt** (`https://api.neuralwatt.com/v1`) as a first-class native provider in Hermes Agent, alongside existing providers like OpenRouter, DeepSeek, and Z.AI.

Neuralwatt is an OpenAI-compatible API that hosts 14 models from multiple families (GLM 5.x, Kimi K2.5/K2.6/K2.7, Qwen 3.5/3.6, MiniMax M2.5, Devstral, gpt-oss-20b). It is already listed on [models.dev](https://models.dev/providers/neuralwatt) and integrated by [Mastra](https://mastra.ai/models/providers/neuralwatt).

## Motivation

Neuralwatt currently works as a "custom" provider by manually setting `model.provider: custom`, `model.base_url`, and `model.api_key` in `config.yaml`. However, this means:

1. **No `hermes model` picker entry** — users must edit config YAML manually to switch to Neuralwatt
2. **No credential pool support** — the API key can't be managed via `hermes auth` or rotated with other keys
3. **No env var convention** — other providers have a standard `*_API_KEY` env var (e.g. `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`); Neuralwatt needs `NEURALWATT_API_KEY`
4. **No `hermes setup` integration** — the setup wizard doesn't offer Neuralwatt as an option
5. **No automatic model discovery** — the `/v1/models` endpoint returns rich metadata (pricing, capabilities, limits) that could power the model picker

## Proposed Solution

Register Neuralwatt as a native provider with:

| Aspect | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Provider ID | `neuralwatt` |
| Base URL | `https://api.neuralwatt.com/v1` |
| API key env var | `NEURALWATT_API_KEY` |
| Auth | Bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`) |
| API format | OpenAI-compatible (`/chat/completions`, `/models`) |
| Setup command | `hermes auth add neuralwatt` |
| Model picker | `hermes model` → Neuralwatt listed |

### Implementation notes

Neuralwatt's API is fully OpenAI-compatible, so the implementation should be minimal — similar to how DeepSeek or Z.AI are integrated:

1. **`hermes_cli/config.py`** — Add `neuralwatt` to the provider registry with:
   - `NEURALWATT_API_KEY` env var mapping
   - Base URL: `https://api.neuralwatt.com/v1`
   - Default model: `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` (or `glm-5-fast` for a cheaper default)

2. **`hermes model` / setup wizard** — Add Neuralwatt to the interactive provider list

3. **Credential pooling** — Register so `hermes auth add neuralwatt` stores the key in `auth.json` and `hermes auth list neuralwatt` retrieves it

4. **Model discovery (optional)** — Neuralwatt's `/v1/models` returns extended metadata per model:
   ```json
   {
     "id": "zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8",
     "metadata": {
       "display_name": "GLM 5.1",
       "capabilities": { "tools": true, "reasoning": true, "json_mode": true, "streaming": true },
       "limits": { "max_context_length": 202752, "max_output_tokens": 16384 },
       "pricing": { "input_per_million": 0.35, "output_per_million": 1.38 }
     }
   }
   ```
   This could populate the model picker with friendly names, capability badges, and pricing.

## Available Models (as of June 2026)

| Model ID | Context | Tools | Reasoning | Input $/M | Output $/M |
|----------|---------|-------|-----------|------------|------------|
| `glm-5.2` | 1M | ✅ | ✅ | $1.45 | $4.50 |
| `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` | 203K | ✅ | ✅ | $1.10 | $3.60 |
| `glm-5-fast` | 203K | ✅ | ❌ | $1.10 | $3.60 |
| `glm-5.1-fast` | 203K | ✅ | ❌ | $1.10 | $3.60 |
| `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5` | 262K | ✅ | ✅ | $0.52 | $2.59 |
| `kimi-k2.5-fast` | 262K | ✅ | ❌ | $0.52 | $2.59 |
| `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6` | 262K | ✅ | ✅ | $0.69 | $3.22 |
| `kimi-k2.6-fast` | 262K | ✅ | ❌ | $0.69 | $3.22 |
| `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code` | 262K | ✅ | ✅ | $0.95 | $4.00 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5` | 197K | ✅ | ✅ | $0.35 | $1.00 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` | 262K | ✅ | ✅ | $0.69 | $4.14 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` | 131K | ✅ | ✅ | $0.29 | $1.15 |
| `mistralai/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512` | 262K | ✅ | ❌ | $0.12 | $0.35 |
| `openai/gpt-oss-20b` | 16K | ✅ | ✅ | $0.03 | $0.16 |

## Alternatives Considered

- **Keep using `custom` provider** — works today but lacks first-class UX (no model picker, no credential pooling, no env var convention). Acceptable as a stopgap but not ideal for discoverability.
- **Route through OpenRouter** — many (but not all) Neuralwatt models are available via OpenRouter. Direct integration avoids double-hop latency and gives access to Neuralwatt-exclusive models like `glm-5.2`.

## References

- Neuralwatt API docs: https://portal.neuralwatt.com/docs/api/models
- models.dev listing: https://models.dev/providers/neuralwatt
- Mastra integration: https://mastra.ai/models/providers/neuralwatt
- Provider is OpenAI-compatible (uses `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` package)

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway exits 1 on cron-triggered LLM IndexError; second crash leaves it down indefinitely (Feishu websocket dies)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

`hermes-gateway` service silently dies when a **cron-scheduled job** calls the LLM and the provider returns a malformed response (manifests as `IndexError: list index out of range`). systemd's `Restart=always` brings it back up the first time, but the same error recurs within ~16 minutes, and the second crash does **NOT** trigger systemd auto-restart — leaving the gateway down indefinitely until manual `hermes gateway restart`.

While the gateway is down, **all connected messaging platforms lose their websocket** (Feishu/Telegram/Discord) and users cannot reach the agent at all.

This bug is **distinct from** but related to:
- #42126 — `gateway run` exits 1 right after platforms connect (crash at startup, not after a cron LLM call)
- #10616 — Feishu WebSocket drops leave zombie gateway without auto-recovery (different trigger, same end-state)

The distinguishing factor of this report: **trigger is a cron-scheduled LLM call**, not gateway startup, not a platform event.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes Agent v0.16.0 with provider `minimax-cn` (Anthropic-compatible endpoint, model `MiniMax-M3`).
2. `hermes gateway restart`.
3. Trigger any cron job that calls the LLM (e.g. the `工作日工作简报` job at 09:00 or `每日中午12点Bitable反向同步` at 12:00).
4. When the provider returns a malformed response the SDK cannot parse, hermes's `agent.conversation_loop` catches `IndexError`, retries 3x, then exits the process.
5. systemd relaunches once (PID changes). The next cron invocation hits the same provider error, gateway crashes again — but this time systemd marks the unit as `failed` and does **not** auto-restart, even though the unit has `Restart=always` and `StartLimitIntervalSec=0`.

## Expected Behavior

1. **Transient API errors should not exit the gateway process.** A failed cron LLM call should log the error and continue — not tear down the gateway (which kills the Feishu/Telegram websocket for ALL concurrent users).
2. **The gateway should not enter a crash-loop on the same error.** Either rate-limit restarts, or stay up and report the cron job as failed via the delivery system.
3. **If the gateway does go down, the user should be notified** (via any working channel) — currently the failure is completely silent. (Partially related to #10616.)

## Actual Behavior

Observed in `journalctl --user -u hermes-gateway` on 2026-06-18:

​```
Jun 18 09:00:41 python[62983]: WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=InternalServerError ... summary=HTTP 500: unknown error, 999 (1000)
Jun 18 09:02:06 python[62983]: ⚠️  API call failed (attempt 1/3): IndexError
...
Jun 18 09:02:06 python[62983]: ❌ API failed after 3 retries — list index out of range
Jun 18 09:02:07 systemd[393]: hermes-gateway.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Jun 18 09:02:14 systemd[321]: Started hermes-gateway.service.   ← systemd restart OK
Jun 18 09:18:59 systemd[393]: Stopping hermes-gateway.service.  ← second crash
Jun 18 09:18:59 systemd[393]: hermes-gateway.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
                                                       ↑ no follow-up "Started" line = gateway stays down
​```

Gateway was down from **09:18 to 12:15** (≈2h56min) before manual `hermes gateway restart`. During this window, the user's Feishu messages had no response because the websocket was dead.

## Root Cause (best guess)

- `IndexError: list index out of range` is raised inside hermes's `agent.conversation_loop` when parsing the LLM response (likely a `tool_use` / `content` array). The exception is caught and retried 3x, but on final failure the conversation loop exits non-zero, which propagates up and tears down the gateway process.
- The malformed-response source appears to be the `minimax-cn` provider returning data the Anthropic SDK can't parse (likely missing or truncated `content` / `tool_use` blocks). Hermes should treat this as a per-job failure and continue, not exit the gateway.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (upstream 95715dcb), Python 3.11.15
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, systemd user service
- Provider: `minimax-cn` (Anthropic-compatible, base URL `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`), model `MiniMax-M3`
- OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
- Connected messaging platform: Feishu (Lark)
- Unit config: `Restart=always`, `RestartSec=5`, `RestartForceExitStatus=75`, `StartLimitIntervalSec=0`

## Debug Report

- Report: https://paste.rs/0rMxL
- agent.log: https://dpaste.com/DBJLYZZVV
- gateway.log: https://dpaste.com/79FJGLJ4F

(Will auto-delete in 6 hours — please fetch promptly.)

## Workaround (in place locally)

A `cron` watchdog every 5 minutes:
​```
*/5 * * * * systemctl --user is-active hermes-gateway || hermes gateway restart
​```
Not a real fix — just keeps the user connected at the cost of repeated restarts.

items.title: [Bug]: `billing_provider` / `billing_base_url` are write-once via COALESCE — mid-session `/model` switch leaves stale provider in session DB and misleads dashboard model cards

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
# [Bug]: `billing_provider` / `billing_base_url` are write-once via COALESCE — mid-session `/model` switch leaves stale provider in session DB and misleads dashboard model cards

## Summary

The session database records `billing_provider` and `billing_base_url` using `COALESCE(column, ?)`, making them **write-once** — the first value written at session creation is permanently locked. When a user switches models mid-session via `/model`, the runtime (`agent.provider`, `agent.base_url`) updates correctly, but the session row never reflects the new provider. This causes the dashboard Models page to display a provider badge that looks like a model/provider compatibility claim when it is really stale historical provenance, and it misattributes token usage / cost analytics to the wrong provider.

## Environment

- **Hermes Agent:** v0.16.0 (commit `5e01a5db`, 2026-06-17)
- **Platform:** Telegram gateway (also affects CLI sessions)
- **Host OS:** Ubuntu 24.04
- **Providers in use:** ollama-cloud, openai-codex, custom (Requesty)

## Root Cause

`hermes_state.py`, `update_token_counts()` method, line ~1568:

```python
# hermes_state.py — update_token_counts(), absolute branch (line ~1568):
billing_provider = COALESCE(billing_provider, ?),
billing_base_url = COALESCE(billing_base_url, ?),
billing_mode = COALESCE(billing_mode, ?),
model = COALESCE(model, ?),

# The incremental branch (line ~1589) has the same COALESCE pattern:
billing_provider = COALESCE(billing_provider, ?),
billing_base_url = COALESCE(billing_base_url, ?),
billing_mode = COALESCE(billing_mode, ?),
model = COALESCE(model, ?),
```

Both the `absolute=True` (gateway) and incremental (CLI) code paths are affected.

The `COALESCE` guard means billing fields are only written when the column is `NULL`. Once the session row is created (at session start, with the initial provider), subsequent `update_token_counts()` calls — including those after a `/model` switch — pass the *new* provider/model values, but `COALESCE` silently discards them because the columns are already populated.

Notably, the maintainers already recognized this COALESCE problem for the `model` column and added `update_session_model()` (`hermes_state.py:1505`) — an unconditional `UPDATE sessions SET model = ? WHERE id = ?` — called from `gateway/slash_commands.py` after `/model` succeeds. But no equivalent method exists for `billing_provider`, `billing_base_url`, or `billing_mode`.

The runtime swap in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:switch_model()` correctly updates `agent.model`, `agent.provider`, `agent.base_url`, and `agent.api_mode`. The next `update_token_counts()` call in `agent/conversation_loop.py` (line ~1873) passes the updated runtime values:

```python
agent._session_db.update_token_counts(
    agent.session_id,
    ...
    billing_provider=agent.provider,   # ← has the new provider after /model switch
    billing_base_url=agent.base_url,   # ← has the new base_url
    model=agent.model,                  # ← has the new model name
    ...
)
```

But `COALESCE` on the DB side means the new values are ignored.

## Impact

### 1. Dashboard Models page — incorrect provider badges

The Models page (`/api/analytics/models`) groups sessions by `model, billing_provider`. A single session that started on one provider and was switched to another shows up under the *original* provider's card, not the one actually used for the API calls.

### 2. Token usage / cost misattribution

All token counts and API call counts for the switched session are attributed to the original provider. This inflates one provider's usage metrics and deflates the other's.

### 3. Multiple provider cards for the same model

The same model (e.g. `gpt-5.4`) appears as separate cards under different providers, making it look like the model was used independently on each provider when in reality some sessions were switched mid-stream.

## Evidence

Real session data from `~/.hermes/state.db`:

### Example: gpt-5.5 attributed to ollama-cloud

A session started on minimax-m3 (ollama-cloud), then switched to gpt-5.5 via `/model`. The session row shows:

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| session_id | `20260613_182640_9b996660` |
| model | `gpt-5.5` |
| billing_provider | `ollama-cloud` |
| billing_base_url | `https://ollama.com/v1` |
| input_tokens | 3,159,099 |
| output_tokens | 16,206 |
| api_call_count | 65 |
| message_count | 147 |

The `model` field *is* updated after a switch — but only because a separate method, `update_session_model()` (`hermes_state.py:1505`), unconditionally overwrites it. That method is called from `gateway/slash_commands.py` (lines 1181 and 1334) after `/model` succeeds. The billing fields (`billing_provider`, `billing_base_url`, `billing_mode`) have no equivalent unconditional update path, so they remain locked to the session-creation value. This is a known pattern the maintainers already solved for `model` but missed for billing fields.

All other gpt-5.5 sessions on this installation correctly show `openai-codex` / `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`.

### Same pattern for gpt-5.4

gpt-5.4 sessions appear under three different providers, including `ollama-cloud` sessions that should be `openai-codex`:

| Date | Provider | Base URL | Msgs | Title |
|------|----------|----------|------|-------|
| 06-16 16:49 | ollama-cloud | https://ollama.com/v1 | 33 | Critique of 5G Network Architecture |
| 06-16 12:06 | openai-codex | https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex | 5 | Relay Mechanisms in 5G Core |
| 06-16 11:42 | custom | https://router.requesty.ai/v1 | 28 | 5G Core Network Relay Architecture |
| 06-13 20:46 | ollama-cloud | https://ollama.com/v1 | 89 | Relay Mechanisms in 5G Core |

The `ollama-cloud` sessions for gpt-5.4 were switched from an ollama-cloud model mid-session.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a session with model A on provider X (e.g. minimax-m3 on ollama-cloud)
2. Mid-session, run `/model <model-B>` where model B is on a different provider Y (e.g. gpt-5.5 on openai-codex)
3. Continue the conversation for several turns
4. Open the dashboard Models page
5. Observe: model B appears under provider X (wrong), not provider Y (correct)
6. Query the session DB directly:
   ```sql
   SELECT id, model, billing_provider, billing_base_url
   FROM sessions WHERE id = '<session-id>';
   ```
   The `billing_provider` and `billing_base_url` still show provider X's values.

## Proposed Fix

### Option A: Overwrite billing fields on model switch (minimal, follows existing precedent)

The maintainers already solved this exact pattern for `model` with `update_session_model()`. This proposal extends the same approach to billing fields: add an `update_billing_info()` method to `SessionDB` that unconditionally writes `billing_provider`, `billing_base_url`, `billing_mode`, and `model`, and call it from `switch_model()`:

```python
# hermes_state.py — new method
def update_billing_info(self, session_id, model, billing_provider, billing_base_url, billing_mode=None):
    self._insert_session_row(session_id, "unknown", model=model)
    self._conn.execute("""
        UPDATE sessions SET
            model = ?,
            billing_provider = ?,
            billing_base_url = ?,
            billing_mode = COALESCE(?, billing_mode)
        WHERE id = ?
    """, (model, billing_provider, billing_base_url, billing_mode, session_id))
    self._conn.commit()
```

```python
# agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py — in switch_model(), after successful swap
if hasattr(agent, '_session_db') and agent._session_db and agent.session_id:
    agent._session_db.update_billing_info(
        agent.session_id,
        model=new_model,
        billing_provider=new_provider,
        billing_base_url=base_url or agent.base_url,
    )
```

### Option B: Remove COALESCE from update_token_counts (broader)

Replace `COALESCE(billing_provider, ?)` with a direct `billing_provider = ?` in `update_token_counts()`. This is simpler but means the billing fields are overwritten on every API call (which is fine — they should reflect the current provider for that call).

**Caveat:** This would only capture the provider of the *last* API call in the session, not per-turn granularity. For sessions with multiple mid-session switches, earlier segments are still lost. Option A is more targeted.

### Option C: Per-turn billing records (most complete, larger scope)

Write a per-API-call billing record (model + provider + base_url + tokens) to a separate table, and aggregate at query time. This is the most accurate but requires a schema migration and dashboard query changes. Referenced as a known gap in issue #28984.

## Possibly Related Issues

- **#37621** — [Bug] Model switch via Telegram `/model` fails to apply to active session (P1 High). Different bug — the switch doesn't take effect at all. But both issues share the same root area: `/model` switch not fully propagating to session state.
- **#28984** — Typed Config-Runtime Contract. Explicitly cites "Per-model token usage lost during /model switch" as a known sub-pattern of the broader config-runtime binding gap.
- **#45715** — Credential pool mismatch: `agent.provider` resolves to bare 'custom'. Related to provider identity confusion, different layer.

items.body:
## Bug Description

When using GLM 5.2 via the `opencode-go` provider, Hermes fails with a non-retryable HTTP 400 error because the internal `timestamp` field is being sent as part of the `messages` array in the API request. GLM's API has strict schema validation and rejects unknown fields.

```
❌ Non-retryable error (HTTP 400): HTTP 400: Error from provider: Extra inputs are not permitted, field: messages[13].timestamp, value: 1781762291.128
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `opencode-go` as the provider with `glm-5.2` as the model
2. Start a conversation and send several messages (enough to build conversation history)
3. Observe the HTTP 400 error on a subsequent turn

## Expected Behavior

Hermes should strip internal fields (`timestamp`, and other non-standard fields) from all outgoing API messages for all providers, not just specific ones.

## Actual Behavior

The `timestamp` field (stored in Hermes's SQLite session store on every message) is leaked into the outgoing API payload. GLM's strict schema validation rejects it with HTTP 400.

## Environment

- **Model**: `glm-5.2`
- **Provider**: `opencode-go`
- **Hermes Version**: v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream c276b017
- **OS**: macOS 26.5.1
- **Python**: 3.11.15
- **OpenAI SDK**: 2.24.0

## Root Cause Analysis

Hermes stores a `timestamp` field on every message in its SQLite session store (`hermes_state.py`):

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
    ...
    timestamp REAL NOT NULL,
    ...
);
```

When building outgoing API messages, `timestamp` is not universally stripped. Some code paths strip it (e.g., the gateway session-reload path in `gateway/run.py` ~line 5295):

```python
clean_msg = {k: v for k, v in msg.items() if k != "timestamp"}
```

But other code paths — particularly the agentic loop in `run_agent.py` — may still pass `timestamp` through to the API request. OpenAI's API silently ignores unknown fields, so this bug is invisible on OpenAI. GLM and other strict-schema providers reject it.

This is the same class of bug as:
- **#134** — Mistral 422 due to extra fields (fixed by PR #138)
- **#893** — `call_id`/`response_item_id` leaked to strict APIs (fixed by PR #5183)
- **#4555** — KV cache invalidation from extra fields in session reload

The `timestamp` field is Hermes-internal metadata, not part of the OpenAI Chat Completions spec, and should never be sent to any provider.

## Proposed Fix

Strip `timestamp` (and other known internal fields) universally when building outgoing API messages, regardless of provider or code path. This should be done in a centralized location (e.g., `_build_api_kwargs()` or a shared sanitization function) rather than piecemeal per provider.

Known internal fields that should be stripped:
- `timestamp`
- `finish_reason` (already stripped in some paths)
- `call_id` (already stripped for some providers via #5183)
- `response_item_id` (already stripped for some providers via #5183)
- `codex_reasoning_items`
- `codex_message_items`
- `reasoning` (converted to `reasoning_content` in some paths)
- `reasoning_details`
- `token_count`

A single `_sanitize_message_for_api()` function called before every API request would eliminate this entire class of bug.

## Related Issues

- #134 — Mistral 422 from extra fields (same root cause, different field/provider)
- #893 — `call_id`/`response_item_id` leaked to strict APIs
- #4555 — Extra fields causing KV cache invalidation
- #26881 — Feature request for `skip_parameters` config for provider API quirks

items.title: Hermes Desktop: vision_analyze ignores config.yaml — Electron main process has hardcoded env defaults

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

In the Hermes Desktop (Electron) build, the `vision_analyze` tool ignores changes to `config.yaml`'s `auxiliary.vision.model` setting. The Electron main process has a baked-in environment that is set at app launch and not refreshed when config is changed.

## Reproduction

1. Set `auxiliary.vision.model: gemma4:31b-cloud` (or any other valid model) in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
2. Launch Hermes Desktop. Inspect the running Electron main process env: it shows `AUXILIARY_VISION_MODEL=qwen3-vl:235b-instruct` (the previous default, or whatever was set at build time), not the config value.
3. Call `vision_analyze`. It tries to use the baked-in model. If that model has been retired (as happened to me with `qwen3-vl:235b-instruct` on 2026-06-16), every call returns a 410.

## What I tried

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| Edit `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (`auxiliary.vision.model`) | ✗ No effect on running Electron main |
| `launchctl setenv AUXILIARY_VISION_MODEL gemma4:31b-cloud` in user domain | ✗ Set successfully (`launchctl getenv` confirms) but does NOT propagate to running GUI app |
| `pkill -9 -f Hermes.app` + relaunch | ✗ App respawns with same baked-in env |
| Search Electron source (`main.cjs`, `dist/`, `app.asar`) for vision default strings (`qwen3-vl`, `AUXILIARY_VISION`) | ✗ Strings not present — vision defaults are baked into compiled binary, not source we can patch |
| Set env var + relaunch from terminal with `open -a Hermes` | ✗ GUI apps on modern macOS don't inherit terminal env cleanly; Electron main retains its launch-time env |

## Diagnosis

The Electron main process is the one that handles in-chat `vision_analyze`. Its env appears to be set at build time (or first launch) and persisted into the running process tree, so:

- `config.yaml` edits have no effect on it
- `launchctl setenv` doesn't propagate (Apple removed user-domain env propagation to GUI apps)
- The strings aren't in the visible source — they look baked into the binary
- The Python gateway process (`auxiliary_bridge.py`) reads `config.yaml` correctly, but the Electron main does not appear to go through the bridge for vision config

## Expected behavior

`config.yaml` `auxiliary.vision.*` should be the source of truth. Changing the model there should be picked up by:
- (a) Reading the config at app startup, OR
- (b) Watching the config and refreshing the in-process env, OR
- (c) Going through the Python gateway bridge that already exists for other auxiliary settings.

The bridge code (in the Python gateway) already handles this for other `auxiliary.*` sections — see the `auxiliary.vision` → `AUXILIARY_VISION_*` env mapping in the bridge. The Electron main just doesn't call into it.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop: latest as of 2026-06-18
- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (Tahoe) on Apple Silicon
- `~/.hermes/config.yaml` `auxiliary.vision` block is correctly populated
- Raw `curl` to the model endpoint works perfectly — the issue is purely that the Electron process uses a different config source

## Workaround

For now I'm routing vision through the Python gateway (calling ollama-cloud directly with the config value), bypassing `vision_analyze`. Functional but slow. Filing this so future users with vendor-retired models don't get stuck.
